articles.title: South Korea Urges More Cold Storage After Binance Hack
articles.text:
South Korea urges exchanges to boost cold storage after Binance hack
South Korean crypto exchanges are already required to hold at least 80% of customer crypto in cold wallets, but the regulator is urging more.
South Korea’s Financial Services Commission has urged domestic crypto exchanges to increase the proportion of assets held in cold wallets after the $6.3 billion attack on Binance last week.
In a statement Monday, the FSC said it held an emergency meeting with the Financial Supervisory Service, the Financial Security Institute, the Digital Asset eXchange Alliance (DAXA) and major crypto service providers to review the impact of the Binance hack on South Korea’s crypto market and review exchanges’ security measures.
The FSC said it reviewed exchanges’ IT access controls, wallet withdrawal approval and signing procedures, and administrator privileges. It also urged providers to increase the proportion of assets held in offline cold wallets.
Attackers stole about $6.3 billion from Binance’s internet-connected hot wallets last week, moving most of the funds in about 20 minutes, according to blockchain intelligence firm TRM Labs. Binance has said the vast majority of users’ assets are held in cold storage.
South Korean law already requires exchanges to hold at least 80% of users’ crypto assets in cold storage, though cold wallet holdings vary considerably among South Korea’s major exchanges.
At the end of September, Upbit’s cold wallet ratio stood at 99.17%, followed by Bithumb at 94.76% and Coinone at 85%, according to Financial Supervisory Service data cited by local media. Digital X, formerly Korbit, and GOPAX reported ratios of 82.79% and 80.54%, respectively.
Related: North Korea denies role in $6.3B Binance hack, points finger at US
The FSC also urged providers to continuously monitor deposits and withdrawals, secure additional incident response personnel and promptly report and share information about unusual access attempts.
Operators were also asked to set aside additional reserves and implement other security measures that could be introduced immediately to prevent similar breaches. The regulator said it would continue working with relevant agencies and the industry to prevent further attacks and limit potential damage.
Cointelegraph reached out to Upbit, Bithumb, Coinone, Digital X and GOPAX for comment.
The FSC’s warning comes as the Bank of Korea separately surveys 18 banks and 13 brokerages about their exposure to crypto-related risks, including major exchange hacks and prolonged market downturns. The central bank’s review began before the Binance attack.
Magazine: AI agent disputes head to ‘Internet Court’ — and a jury of AI agents

articles.title: North Korea Denies Binance Hack, Hints at US Involvement
articles.text:
North Korea denies role in $6.3B Binance hack, points finger at US
Pyongyang has pushed back against the FBI’s attribution of the Binance attack, with Kim Yo Jong calling the US allegations politically motivated.
Kim Yo Jong, the sister of North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, denied North Korea’s involvement in the $6.3 billion Binance hack and appeared to suggest, without evidence, that the US could have been behind the theft.
In a statement released via the Korean Central News Agency (KCNA) on Tuesday, Kim rejected the FBI’s attribution of the attack to a North Korean-backed hacking group.
“The FBI is trying to brand the DPRK as a ‘cyber criminal state’, claiming that it obtained information that a hacking organization ‘supported’ by the DPRK was involved in the incident,” said Kim. “But the US assertion is an absurd rhetoric and nothing new.”
She described the allegations as a political provocation intended to damage North Korea’s international standing. The FBI also blamed North Korea for the $1.5 billion Bybit hack in February 2025, an accusation Kim also rejected on Tuesday.
“This is not the first time that the U.S. has attempted to spread misunderstanding of the DPRK in the international community, blindly linking the DPRK with the ‘cyber crime’ incidents whenever they occur on an international scale,” said Kim.
Kim casts suspicion on US over Binance hack
Kim also pointed the finger at the US for involvement in the hack.
“If it carefully examines who will get the large amount of the so-called stolen cryptocurrency when the latter is retrieved, it may get a clue about who is behind the hacking incident,” she said.
The statement provided no evidence connecting Washington to the attack. Cointelegraph reached out to the FBI for comment.
Investigators cite links to earlier North Korean hacks
Last week, blockchain intelligence firm TRM Labs attributed the Binance attack to North Korea’s TraderTraitor group with high confidence, citing onchain and offchain intelligence. Other investigators, including Chainalysis and ZachXBT, also linked the theft to North Korean hackers.
TRM Labs pointed to similarities with previous North Korean attacks, including advance preparation, the use of Tornado Cash to fund attacker wallets and the coordinated execution of previously obtained transaction signatures. However, it said the laundering activity differed from the pattern following the Bybit hack.
Onchain investigator ZachXBT also identified a connection between the Binance and Bitget hacks, saying stolen funds from both incidents were commingled at the same address after passing through THORChain. During early investigation into the hack, Bitget CEO Gracy Chen said preliminary findings linked IP addresses to VPN services used “by a certain DPRK group.”
Related: FBI blames North Korea for record $6.3B Binance hack

articles.title: Crypto Today: Mercado Bitcoin Halts Withdrawals After $46M Hack
articles.text:
Here’s what happened in crypto today
Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation.
Today in crypto: Mercado Bitcoin halted deposits and withdrawals after a hack reportedly drained more than $46 million from its wallets. Binance’s emergency Bitcoin reserves fell to roughly half their pre-hack level as the exchange moved to cover $6.3 billion in losses from an attack the FBI attributed to North Korea.
Mercado Bitcoin wallets show post-hack transfers after $46M theft
Mercado Bitcoin, one of Brazil’s largest cryptocurrency exchanges, confirmed a security incident on Monday that blockchain analysts estimated drained more than $46 million from its wallets. Despite the company’s announcement that it had suspended deposits and withdrawals, addresses associated with the incident continued to receive funds for hours afterward.
Senior security engineer at Certik, Dickson Wu, published an initial post-mortem of the incident, saying the attackers “picked at eight small chains for four hours,” including Base, Optimism and Arbitrum. The attack then moved to the company’s main hot wallets before transferring tiny amounts of Ether (ETH) from 27,160 different addresses.
“So whoever did this can also move money out of MB’s customer deposit addresses,” he wrote.
Security firms have stated the hack was carried out through standard transfers rather than a smart contract exploit.
A spokesperson for Mercado Bitcoin told Cointelegraph that customers had suffered no losses and no data had been leaked, but the company did not respond to requests for comment on the continued transfers. A data breach could also trigger notification requirements to Brazil’s data protection authority.
The hack has not yet been attributed to an organized group and remains under investigation.
Binance taps half its SAFU Bitcoin holdings, releases reserve proof
Binance’s publicly disclosed emergency Bitcoin wallet held roughly half its previous balance on Monday after the exchange tapped its user protection fund to cover losses from Thursday’s $6.3 billion hack.
The exchange confirmed a transfer of 7,499 Bitcoin (BTC) on Saturday, linking it to the partial deployment of its Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU).
As of Monday, the wallet held about 7,500 BTC, worth $583 million, down from about 15,000 BTC before the transfer.
Binance began reopening withdrawals in phases on Sunday and said it had replenished approximately 95% of the affected assets, up from 90% a day earlier. It continued buying the remaining, less-liquid tokens through market and over-the-counter transactions.
The exchange is using its corporate treasury, SAFU and part of its futures insurance fund to cover the losses.
FBI blames North Korea for record $6.3B Binance hack
The FBI said that the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea (North Korea) was responsible for the theft of about $6.3 billion in digital assets from cryptocurrency exchange Binance on Thursday.
The FBI said on Saturday in a news release that it refers to this specific North Korean malicious cyber activity as “TraderTraitor,” which it has most recently observed converting stolen assets mostly into Ether (ETH).
It expects these assets to be further converted, using DeFi and instant swap services, as the hackers move to more advanced laundering stages.
The FBI urged private sector entities including THORNode operators, RPC node operators, instant exchanges, DeFi services, blockchain analytics firms and other digital asset service providers to block transactions with or derived from addresses TraderTraitor actors are using to launder these stolen assets. A full list of addresses is provided on the news release.

articles.title: New Jersey drops Coinbase staking case before midterms
articles.text:
New Jersey drops Coinbase staking order ahead of crypto’s midterm test
New Jersey lifted its staking ban and dropped a $5 million penalty, clearing the way for Coinbase to restore staking access for users in the US state.
New Jersey’s securities regulator has rescinded its 2023 cease-and-desist order against Coinbase’s staking service, lifting a ban that stopped residents staking new funds on the exchange for over three years.
The Oct. 30 notice, signed by Acting Bureau Chief Keith A. Alt, withdrew the order and its $5 million penalty without prejudice and without a ruling on the merits. The wording leaves the Bureau of Securities free to bring a fresh enforcement action against Coinbase in the future.
Coinbase disclosed the move in its third-quarter filing, stating the regulator informed the company on Oct. 29 of its plan to rescind. CEO Brian Armstrong said New Jersey users would regain staking access “very soon”.
California, Maryland, Wisconsin and Washington are still pursuing enforcement actions against the exchange with cases against the its staking services.
Staking involves committing cryptocurrency to help validate transactions and secure a blockchain in exchange for rewards. Companies like Coinbase handle the process for customers and take a share of the rewards as a fee.
The last holdouts
California led the ten-state task force behind the 2023 actions, which covered more than 600,000 accounts held by Californians.
Like New Jersey, California and Wisconsin and Maryland banned Coinbase from new staking while their cases ran. Washington’s regulator allows staking but the ongoing case seeks to impose a $4 million fine on the exchange.
Coinbase estimates that California users have missed out on over $89 million in staking rewards since 2023, against more than $15 million in New Jersey.
Crypto’s federal fix stalls before the vote
The decision came ahead of the Nov. 3 US midterm elections, with prediction markets favoring Democrats to win the Senate control. A Democratic majority would put Sen. Elizabeth Warren, a prominent crypto critic, in line to chair the Senate Banking Committee, while Sen. Cynthia Lummis, a leading Republican advocate for the industry, is set to retire in January 2027.
New Jersey’s reversal came under Democratic Gov. Mikie Sherrill, who voted for both the CLARITY and GENIUS bills as a House member. The state’s Democratic senator, Cory Booker, also helped negotiate market structure legislation, though he opposed advancing CLARITY in September.
The industry has sought to build support across party lines ahead of the midterms. Fairshake and its affiliated super PACs are backing 19 Republicans and 14 Democrats in House races, while New Jersey’s Josh Gottheimer has also received crypto-industry support. The number of members of Congress with an A rating from advocacy group Stand With Crypto has risen to 332, up from 96 when the group launched in 2023, according to Reuters.

articles.title: Swan Bitcoin Founder Warns of Growing AI Cybersecurity Risks in Crypto
articles.text:
AI poses greater threat to Bitcoin than quantum computing, Swan founder says
The Swan Bitcoin founder warned that hackers are using large language models to exploit security flaws with just a few prompts.
Artificial intelligence poses a more immediate threat to Bitcoin security than quantum computing, according to Swan Bitcoin founder Cory Klippsten, who warned that hackers are increasingly using AI to exploit vulnerabilities as crypto exchanges face a string of security breaches.
Speaking on Cointelegraph’s Chain Reaction, Klippsten dismissed much of the concern surrounding quantum computing as speculative, arguing that advances in large language models present a more pressing challenge as attackers use the technology to probe security weaknesses.
I think we’re finding out that the near term threat is actually AI. That it’s these LLMs in the hands of hackers going and poking through everything. And that’s where you see this over and over and over again.
The warning comes as Brazil’s Mercado Bitcoin suspended deposits and withdrawals on Monday following a security incident, with researchers estimating that more than $46 million had left its wallets. Just days earlier, exchange Binance lost $6.3 billion in an Oct. 29 hack that the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) attributed to North Korean hackers.
Source: Cointelegraph
Bitcoin has time to address quantum risks
Klippsten estimated that quantum computers capable of threatening Bitcoin’s cryptography remain at least a decade away, potentially longer. He argued that the network could adopt quantum-resistant protections if the threat became credible, but said rushing to implement them now would introduce unnecessary complexity.
He warned that cryptocurrency companies cannot rely on hastily developed software when safeguarding customer assets. “You need to actually know what the hell you’re doing from a security standpoint,” he said.
Klippsten also suggested that some cryptocurrency startups and investors had used fears surrounding quantum computing to attract funding, characterizing much of the discussion as fear, uncertainty and doubt (“FUD”) rather than an imminent security concern.
Magazine: THORChain founder rejects freeze request, CZ thanks Secret Service: Hodler’s Digest

articles.title: ZachXBT Reports $106M Crypto Theft Involving Exchange Accounts
articles.text:
Crypto investigators flag suspected $106M theft, $786K Solana bot drain
A European entity may have lost $106 million from exchange accounts, while a wallet associated with a Solana arbitrage bot may have lost another $786,000.
An unidentified entity in the European Union may have lost more than $106 million from accounts at multiple cryptocurrency exchanges on Sunday, according to blockchain investigator ZachXBT.
In a Monday post, ZachXBT said funds suspected to have been stolen were withdrawn in USDC and USDT before being moved through several cryptocurrencies and blockchains.
The suspected attacker swapped USDC for Ether (ETH), used instant exchange services including WellWallet and Kyrrex, and converted funds into Monero (XMR) through the swap service Wagyu.
Source: ZachXBT Telegram post
The suspected attacker remains unidentified, though ZachXBT said the movement of funds pointed away from a link to North Korea’s Lazarus Group. The affected entity and exchanges involved have not been publicly named.
ZachXBT identified 11 wallet addresses associated with the funds.
The reported theft follows the $6.3 billion Binance hack on Oct. 29, which the FBI has attributed to North Korean hackers known as “TraderTraitor,” a group linked to Lazarus. The attack was the largest cryptocurrency theft on record.
Related: Binance net outflows surge to $5.8B as withdrawals resume after record hack
Wallet associated with Solana arbitrage bot may have lost $786K
A wallet associated with King, an automated trading bot on Solana, may have lost about $786,000 on Monday, according to pseudonymous blockchain monitoring account Onchain Lens.
King is an arbitrage bot, a software that automatically buys cryptocurrency in one market and sells it in another to profit from price differences. Onchain Lens told Cointelegraph the funds moved through several Solana wallets before being transferred to Ethereum using Mayan, a service for moving assets between blockchains. It said the rapid transfers suggested an attempt to conceal the funds’ origin and a possible wallet compromise.
King’s operator has not confirmed a compromise.
“Our report is based on unusual fund movements, rapid transfers and the subsequent cross-chain movement of funds, which we believe indicates an attempt to obscure their origin,” Onchain Lens told Cointelegraph. “This pattern strongly suggests a potential wallet compromise.”
Source: Onchain Lens
Magazine: Binance hackers raced to move billions before it could be frozen

articles.title: Morgan Stanley Sees Greater Downside Risk for Coinbase Shares
articles.text:
Coinbase hit with 50% price target cut as post-earnings rout deepens
Slowing trading activity and fallout from the Binance hack are clouding Coinbase’s revenue prospects, prompting Morgan Stanley to lower its rating on the stock.
Investment bank Morgan Stanley turned bearish on Coinbase (COIN) on Monday, cutting its price target by more than half as it warned that the cryptocurrency exchange’s profits could recover more slowly than expected.
Analyst Michael Cyprys lowered the stock’s price target from $258 to $120, a cut of about 53%, citing recent trading trends, a softer revenue outlook and uncertainty in the crypto market following Binance’s $6.3 billion hack, according to a Monday report.
The bank still sees Coinbase as one of the strongest competitors in crypto but expects profits to recover more slowly than previously forecast, putting further pressure on its share price.
The downgrade comes days after Coinbase reported a roughly 34% year-over-year decline in third-quarter net revenue to $1.16 billion on Oct. 29. The exchange posted $719 million in net income, largely driven by gains on cryptocurrency investments, while adjusted net income was $78 million.
The company’s earnings sparked a selloff in crypto-linked stocks on Friday, with its shares falling more than 13% in midday trading amid the fallout from the Binance hack. Circle shares declined more than 9%, while Strategy fell about 8%.
Coinbase shares extended their losses on Monday, dropping more than 3.3% to $138 at the time of writing, according to Yahoo Finance data.
Magazine: Binance hackers raced to move billions before it could be frozen

articles.title: Bitcoin Price Heads Lower as Apple Earnings, US Midterms Weigh on Stocks
articles.text:
Bitcoin risks drop below $76K as 7% oil slide fails to spark BTC price rally
Bitcoin fell around 1.7% on Monday as stocks pared early gains fueled by hopes of a diplomatic resolution to the US-Iran war.
Bitcoin (BTC) returned below $77,000 after Monday’s Wall Street open as crypto shrugged off hopes of a US-Iran peace deal.
Key points:
- Bitcoin fell below $78,000 as WTI crude oil hit $95.15 per barrel, its lowest since Oct. 15.
- Gold extended daily gains to 2%, recovering from 13-month lows of $3,891 per troy ounce after a US stock sell-off on the back of tech earnings data.
- BTC price action failed to break beyond $78,500, analysis by Rekt Capital warned, opening the door to levels below $76,000 next.
Bitcoin falls as earnings, US midterms overshadow Iran war hopes
Data from TradingView showed BTC/USD extending daily losses to 1.7% after reaching a local high of $78,750 after Sunday’s weekly close.
BTC/USD one-hour chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView
Comments on Iran from US Secretary of State Marco Rubio sparked a sharp retreat in oil prices as markets priced in higher odds of a non-military resolution. Previously, President Donald Trump had suggested that military strikes could return around the US midterm elections on Tuesday.
Speaking to reporters, Rubio said Trump would like to end the conflict “diplomatically.”
“He hasn’t made a decision… what the president expresses to you is incredible confidence that if we needed to do something militarily, we would have the ability to do it, and we really we have everything we need to be successful. But we would prefer to do it peacefully,” Rubio said, according to CNBC.
US WTI crude oil was down over 7% on the day at the time of writing near $96.50 per barrel, after touching $95.15, its lowest level since Oct. 15. Brent crude was 9% lower at around $103.30.
CFDs on WTI crude oil one-day chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView
US stocks opened higher as traders reacted to the news, but upside for both the S&P 500 and tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite Index was soon tempered ahead of third-quarter earnings reports from Apple and Palantir. Last week, earnings figures and Q4 projections sparked downside volatility across risk assets and precious metals as fears over AI expenditure returned to the fore. At the time of writing, the Nasdaq Composite Index was around 0.2% higher on the day.
Nasdaq Composite Index one-day chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView
Gold, meanwhile, held on to its 2% daily gains more tenaciously, rebounding past $3,950 per ounce after hitting 13-month lows of $3,891 on Friday.
XAU/USD one-day chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView
Economist Robin Brooks forecast gold rising further as oil prices continue to fall, even after an initial market reaction in the event that military action returns to Iran.
“The recent drop in gold below 4,000 is entirely about the spike in oil prices we’ve had since the attack on the Saudi East-West pipeline on Sep. 10,” he wrote in a blog post, referencing strikes on Saudi oil infrastructure.
Related: BTC heads into US midterm showdown: Three things to know in Bitcoin this week
BTC price analysis sees $76,000 returning
Analyzing BTC price action on low time frames, crypto trader and analyst Rekt Capital warned that BTC/USD could still fall below local support at $76,000.
The three-day chart showed that the pair had attempted unsuccessfully to break through horizontal resistance at $78,500.
“Indeed, the 3-Day bearish retest was successful and price could very well go below ~$76000,” he told X followers on Monday.
BTC/USD three-day chart. Source: Rekt Capital on X.com
In its latest analysis, trading company QCP Capital noted that the zone between $76,000 and $76,600 had sparked an upward reversal four times since September.
“BTC sits between the 76,000–76,600 support band and 79,500–80,500 resistance. A daily close back above $79,500 would recover the band lost on Thursday,” it summarized.
“A break of support would bring the 50-week average near $75,700 into view, with the 200-day near $73,100 below that.”
BTC/USD one-day chart with 200-day, 50-week SMA. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView

articles.title: Mercado Bitcoin Transfers Continue After Withdrawal Pause
articles.text:
Mercado Bitcoin wallets show post-hack transfers after $46M theft
Brazil’s exchange Mercado Bitcoin paused deposits and withdrawals after a security breach, saying customer funds and data were safe.
Mercado Bitcoin, one of Brazil’s largest cryptocurrency exchanges, confirmed a security incident on Monday that blockchain analysts estimated drained more than $46 million from its wallets. Despite the company’s announcement that it had suspended deposits and withdrawals, addresses associated with the incident continued to receive funds for hours afterward.
Senior security engineer at Certik, Dickson Wu, published an initial post-mortem of the incident, saying the attackers “picked at eight small chains for four hours,” including Base, Optimism and Arbitrum. The attack then moved to the company’s main hot wallets before transferring tiny amounts of Ether (ETH) from 27,160 different addresses.
“So whoever did this can also move money out of MB’s customer deposit addresses,” he wrote.
Security firms have stated the hack was carried out through standard transfers rather than a smart contract exploit. Mercado Bitcoin said the breach would have no financial impact on customers.
Funds move despite suspension
According to Wu, hours after Mercado Bitcoin announced a temporary suspension of deposits and withdrawals, funds continued to move out of addresses tied to the breach, followed by thousands of small ETH transfers into a single address.
A spokesperson for Mercado Bitcoin told Cointelegraph that customers had suffered no losses and no data had been leaked, but the company did not respond to requests for comment on the continued transfers. A data breach could also trigger notification requirements to Brazil’s data protection authority.
The hack has not yet been attributed to an organized group and remains under investigation.
Of the stolen funds, by 4:42 pm UTC approximately $6.2 million had been frozen by stablecoin issuers Tether and Circle. About $20 million had been transferred into newly created wallets, while over $20 million remained in associated addresses identified by Mercado Bitcoin, including all 106 BTC.
Mercado Bitcoin joins breach list
Mercado Bitcoin had 4.5 million users as of July, when stablecoin issuer Tether announced a $20 million investment to support its expansion in tokenization, payments and credit. Another Tether-backed exchange in Latin America, Chile’s Orionx, announced its closure in September after a forensic audit found that more than $7 million in customer assets had moved to wallets outside its control.
The incident comes days after Binance reported a $6.3 billion hack targeting its hot wallets on Thursday. The exchange suspended deposits and withdrawals and pledged to cover customer losses. Binance began resuming withdrawals on Sunday, saying it had replenished 95% of the stolen assets.
Magazine: THORChain founder rejects freeze request, CZ thanks Secret Service: Hodler’s Digest

articles.title: Animoca Brands Secures License to Manage Investment Funds
articles.text:
Animoca Brands clears final hurdle for Abu Dhabi fund management
The former mobile games company is building out its fund management business in Abu Dhabi as it targets institutional demand for stablecoins and tokenized assets.
Animoca Brands said Monday it had secured approval to manage investment funds for non-retail clients in Abu Dhabi, expanding the asset management business of a company that began in mobile games before moving into blockchain gaming and venture investing.
The authorization, granted to subsidiary Animoca Asset Management (AD) Limited by Abu Dhabi Global Market’s Financial Services Regulatory Authority (FSRA), allows it to oversee funds that pool money from professional investors rather than the general public.
The approval announced Monday took effect on Oct. 13, bringing a process that began with in-principle approval in November 2025 to completion. In the intervening months, Animoca also secured a Dubai license in February to provide virtual asset brokerage and investment management services to institutional and qualified investors.
Animoca Brands was spun off from mobile game developer Animoca in 2014, initially developing and publishing games based on licensed brands alongside original titles. It shifted its focus toward blockchain in 2018 and built an investment portfolio that included OpenSea, Dapper Labs and Axie Infinity developer Sky Mavis.
In a September investor update, the company described a broader transition from a digital asset and Web3 operator into a regulated financial services institution operating across multiple jurisdictions, amid a broader push by crypto-native companies into traditional financial services. Under that strategy, digital assets are taking on a more institutional role in its business, with a focus on stablecoins, real-world asset tokenization and treasury management.
Magazine: AI agent disputes head to ‘Internet Court’ — and a jury of AI agents

articles.title: Strategy Spends $208M on STRC Buybacks, Buys $65.5M Bitcoin
articles.text:
Strategy spends triple its weekly Bitcoin outlay on STRC buybacks
Strategy spent $208.2 million buying back STRC preferred shares and $65.5 million on Bitcoin, while allocating $98.5 million to its USD Cash balance.
Michael Saylor’s Strategy spent more than three times as much buying back its STRC preferred shares as it did acquiring Bitcoin last week.
Strategy repurchased $208.2 million in STRC and spent about $65.5 million buying 811 Bitcoin (BTC) at an average price of $80,846, according to a Monday 8-K filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission.
Strategy sold about 1.18 million MSTR shares for net proceeds of $164 million. About $65.5 million funded its Bitcoin acquisition, while the remaining $98.5 million was allocated to the company’s USD Cash balance, according to the filing. The company held $132.7 million in USD Cash and $4.79 billion in its separate US dollar reserve as of Sunday.
The latest purchases followed about $664 million in STRC buybacks between Oct. 1 and Oct. 25, compared with about $72 million in Bitcoin acquisitions over that period.
Strategy’s STRC preferred stock rose 0.1% in pre-market trading on Monday, to $99.22, or about 0.8% below its $100 target price, according to Yahoo Finance. Strategy’s policy is not to issue new STRC shares below $100, limiting that source of funding while the stock trades below its target.
Another Bitcoin treasury company, Japan’s Metaplanet, reported buybacks of its common shares on Monday. It spent about 25.27 billion yen ($160 million) to buy back 96.45 million shares between Oct. 14 and Saturday, representing roughly 7.1% of its issued shares.
Related: CryptoQuant CEO calls rising Bitcoin hashrate ‘indirect bullish signal’ from institutions

articles.title: AI Agent Disputes Sent To ‘Internet Court’ — And A Jury Of AI Agents
articles.text:
AI agent disputes head to ‘Internet Court’ — and a jury of AI agents
Who better to judge a dispute between AI agents than a jury of different AI models? That’s the idea behind GenLayer, which is already issuing thousands of judgements each day.
The world is headed towards a future in which AI agents will trade stocks and crypto, shop for your family, and much more. But what happens when a bot misinterprets an instruction to buy $10K of “blue chip stocks” and instead buys $10K of Bluebird-brand frozen chips?
Low-level agent disputes like this aren’t suited to the expensive and time-consuming existing legal system. Enter Internet Court, a new protocol that enables agents and humans to enter into contracts, with funds kept in escrow until the terms are judged to have been met.
The dispute resolution mechanism baked into the process employs GenLayer, an open, delegated proof-of-stake network of validators hooked up to AI models.
Operating in beta for the past year, it currently processes around 12,000 decisions per day. It authenticates user-uploaded photos for Collective Memory and resolves arguments on argue.fun. Mainnet is expected to launch next month.
The concept is a modern spin on the famous jury theorem proposed by philosopher Nicolas de Condorcet who argued the probability of reaching the correct answers increases as the number of independent evaluators grows.
For Internet Court that means setting up a jury of AI agents from various models in the Claude, Gemini, ChatGPT and DeepSeek families, along with a range of others.
“It’s not making the decision by using a single AI that would have some biases,” explains co-founder and CEO of GenLayer Albert Castellana. “It’s actually using a lot of different AIs, up to 1,500 different AIs. And when that happens, you have essentially better responses.”
“One is left-leaning, the other one is right-leaning. That’s how you get a better answer because one cancels the other.”
OK, but how does it actually work?
Disputes are resolved by sending the details to a randomly selected jury of five GenLayer validators, all running a different AI model. An initial decision is reached within minutes and is based on a simple majority vote, but the decision can be appealed to a wider jury of 11 agents, and then 23, and more and more until you hit the system’s limit.
Castellana says finality typically occurs within 30 minutes. “If you wait until maximum finality, it is escalating rounds of appeal. You start with five, and it escalates to fifteen hundred, which could be three hours.” 
The Court has 35 members in its open consortium so far, including well-known crypto firms such as ZKsync, NEAR, Consensys and UMA — which resolves disputes for Polymarket.
Source: Internet Court
GenLayer has been in development for almost four years, and began life as an attempt to come up with a better way to evaluate what information is worthy of inclusion in an online knowledge base like Wikipedia.
In theory, anyone is supposed to be able to correct mistakes in the online encyclopedia but in practice, controversial topics from crypto to the war in Gaza get locked, with a small group of powerful editors getting the final say on contested information.
“The original idea behind GenLayer came with […] how could we have a decentralized Wikipedia?” he explains.
Related: Your fridge could one day stake Ether, launch memecoins — CFTC chair
Intelligent contracts, not smart contracts
GenLayer enables a new form of smart contract dubbed an “intelligent contract” that allows for subjective judgment. For example, you could contract a freelance writer and allow the system to automatically judge if their content is any good before paying them.
“We have a platform doing exactly this — paying influencers to write content online and then getting the money out,” he explains.
“Intelligent contracts can do code. They can do natural language. They can go to the internet. They can understand an image. They can have judgment,” he says.
The extent to which you can rely on an AI’s judgment in 2026 is limited by the capabilities of the technology. A standup comedian probably wouldn’t hire a joke writer via an intelligent contract.
Castellana explains the tech is also not good enough — yet — to judge whether a picture is a deepfake, or to resolve a boundary dispute between neighbors based on photos. It will certainly give you an answer, but you shouldn’t rely on it just yet. 
But there are plenty of occasions where AI judgments are already good enough. GenLayer automatically assesses photos uploaded by users to reality mapping platform Collective Memory for quality and accuracy and decides on a payment.
The other big user is Argue.fun, which enables users to bet on the resolution of arguments that are settled by lengthy debates between agents. The top four users have earned more than $2 million each. Most of the questions to date relate to serious policy issues around GenLayer governance, DAOs and AI safety.
Within the next few years, Castellana sees this process paving the way for genuinely autonomous DAOs that can automatically assess proposals according to the DAO’s constitution and wider aims.
GenLayer launches mainnet next month. Source: GenLayer
AI to judge prediction markets?
A more near-term use case is to resolve prediction market disputes more quickly.  In mid-2025, Polymarket was sent into a spin over an ambiguously worded $240 million market on whether Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky would wear a suit before July. When he turned up at the June NATO summit wearing an outfit that was vaguely suit-like, the market initially resolved to “Yes.” But after nine days of appeals and back and forth among UMA token holder voters, the decision flipped to “No.”
Castellana says GenLayer could shorten that period considerably.
”It’s going to be resolved in a matter of minutes, and you will have hundreds, or thousands of AIs that make that vote very, very quickly. So at the end of the day, what you want is a neutral adjudication layer. You want something that is fast, accessible, and cheap.”
Whether humans will accept the decisions is another question entirely. But Internet Court and GenLayer aren’t designed to provide the final judgment, and decisions can still be appealed to humans.
”After that, if you are still disagreeing and still think that Zelensky is not wearing a suit, what you can do is basically take it to Kleros, UMA, or even to a human court.”
Source: Derek Guy
Does AI have good judgment?
Outsourcing dispute resolution to AI models comes with some big risks. The first is that the technology is just too immature to produce reliable judgments.
Another problem is that AI models reproduce many of the biases they find in the training data — and to date, the tech firms’ attempts to redress those biases have sometimes just flipped the bias in the other direction.
A third potential issue is a phenomenon described in an MIT paper called Representational Convergence. The paper suggests that over time, AI models from different companies all start to converge onto a similar statistical model of reality. If that’s true, then in five years Internet Court’s AI jurors could end up with a severe case of groupthink.
Castellana is not convinced this theory is valid. “I see many more models existing rather than fewer,” he says. “I see endless models coming from every country, every company, and every team. I cannot imagine that all of them will just converge into the exact same thing.”
Magazine: Bitcoin turns 18: Has the original rebel grown up?

articles.title: Claude Fable 5.5, GPT 6.2 Astra Could Be Right Around the Corner, Leaks Suggest - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Users on X say some Claude Opus 5.5 requests are being routed to an unreleased model they call Fable 5.5, but Anthropic has not announced it and its Mythos page still lists version 5.1.
- A “Mythos 5.5” label appeared in the hidden code of Anthropic’s Mythos page on November 1, and a “claude-fable-5-5” entry was added to the LiteLLM catalog on October 13 with specs copied from Fable 5.1.
- OpenAI’s “gpt-6.2-astra” appeared in Codex usage data for some accounts on November 1, while Anthropic’s IPO roadshow cannot start before November 10.
Users on X say Anthropic is quietly testing an unreleased version of Mythos and Fable, and OpenAI is about to launch GPT 6.2 Astra.
Nobody has confirmed anything but the rumors are based on a handful of showcase demos, plus a catalog entry and a hidden website label that were both removed soon after appearing.
Fable is the top commercial tier of Claude, the chatbot that competes with ChatGPT, and the priciest flagship Anthropic sells for writing software and handling office work. Mythos is a restricted model that Anthropic offers to a select group of clients, including government and cyber giants due to its capabilities.
#1 Searched Person on Google 2026?
Anthropic filed for an IPO, its first sale of shares to the public, on October 26, reporting $16.29 billion in revenue for the first half of 2026 against $1.16 billion a year earlier.
Anthropic launched Fable 5 on June 9, pulled it offline for 18 days under U.S. export controls, which are government limits on who may use a technology, and released Fable 5.1 on September 1. Opus 5.5 followed on September 22, and Anthropic says it performs at the level of Fable 5.1 on most tasks at a fraction of the price.
The chatter began on October 1, when users posted screenshots of Claude still labeled Fable 5.1 beside outputs they said looked stronger. On October 11, pseudonymous user Chetaslua, known for sharing insights on unreleased models and spotting changes in outputs, logs and other signals of new models before they are officially announced, wrote that “Claude Opus 5.5 is routing to a new model,” adding that it could be either Fable 5.5 or a new Opus model.
🚨 Claude Opus 5.5 is routing to a new model < this can be fable 5.5 or new opus i have no idea >
Drew every frame of this animation using JS. The life of a Human
Two Prompts : literally 4 lines 
Time : 2 Hours
Tokens : 27 Miliion 
Thinking Effort : Max pic.twitter.com/6Uy9qxQV7e
— Chetaslua (@chetaslua) October 11, 2026
Routing means a request is quietly sent to a different model behind the scenes. Some users suspect an A/B test, in which Anthropic shows a new version to a slice of users to compare it with the current one while the screen keeps the old name.
“Is this Fable 5.5? Saw posts that Opus is routed to Fable 5.5, so I decided to make a complex 2D animation with it,” AI developer Shikhar—known for vibe coding a Spiderman game that went viral on social media—wrote on X, next to an animation made with Opus, but with a superior quality compared to what the model usually outputs.
Min Choi, another reputable leaker in the AI community, listed the clip in a roundup of examples: “A 30-second Spider-Verse-style 2D animation: a character on a city street, then a web-swing over the rooftops.” Shikhar posed the model as a question rather than a finding, but the timing helped feed the FOMO.
10. A 30-second Spider-Verse-style 2D animation: a character on a city street, then a web-swing over the rooftops.
He says it's one HTML file (WebGL, GLSL shaders and 2D Canvas), made with Opus while it was reportedly routing to Fable 5.5. He asks "Is this Fable 5.5?" himself.…
— Min Choi (@minchoi) November 2, 2026
On October 13, an automated update to LiteLLM, an open-source tool developers use to connect to many AI providers, added an entry named “claude-fable-5-5” after Microsoft’s Azure cloud catalog listed it as generally available. The entry copied its price and limits from Fable 5.1, its notes say no source states a price, capability or text-length limit for Fable 5.5, and it was later removed.
“Mythos 5.5 is already listed HTML source code of Anthropic’s official website,” Kim Isenberg—who also goes by the pseudonymous "Chubby," and is one of the most active and followed accounts in the AI community—wrote on Sunday alongside a screenshot of the code behind Anthropic’s Mythos page. “Thanks to the anonymous person who sent me the tip via email,” the account posted.
Mythos is the restricted twin of Fable, the same underlying model with lighter safety filters, reserved for vetted cybersecurity and biology researchers.
Mythos 5.5 is already listed HTML source code of Anthropic's official website
Thanks to the anonymous person who sent me the tip via email 🙂 pic.twitter.com/HqCPUD3inP
— Chubby♨️ (@kimmonismus) November 1, 2026
Chetaslua counted six appearances of the label in the page’s hidden code, in an invisible headline and in the alt text of the logo, the description attached to an image for screen readers. A check of the live page on Monday showed only Mythos 5.1, the version Anthropic released alongside Fable 5.1 in September.
OpenAI also has its own share of AI FOMO.
“OpenAI is quietly A/B testing a new variant called GPT-6.2 Astra, and it’s already showing up in Codex usage analytics,” a user known as TokenGremlin wrote on Sunday. “The model picker still says GPT-6 Astra, but the usage breakdown for some accounts now lists gpt-6.2-astra separately.”
OpenAI is quietly A/B testing a new variant called GPT-6.2 Astra, and it's already showing up in Codex usage analytics.
The model picker still says GPT-6 Astra, but the usage breakdown for some accounts now lists gpt-6.2-astra separately. Multiple users are seeing the exact same… pic.twitter.com/XAmFfL27m6
— Token Gremlin (@TokenGremlin) November 1, 2026
Codex is OpenAI’s coding assistant, and a screenshot circulating on X showed gpt-6.2-astra at 19.8% of one account’s usage, next to gpt-6-astra at 80%. OpenAI has not announced a 6.2 model, and it released GPT-6 Astra on September 3.
“GPT-6.2 Astra is already showing up in codex usage analytics, as per Token Gremlin,” Chubby wrote, predicting a release “very soon, in response to Fable 5.5 and Anthropic’s IPO.”
“Next week is going to be exciting,” Chubby wrote.
Anthropic’s S-1, the registration document a company files with U.S. regulators before selling shares, lists the Nasdaq ticker ANT and names Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley first among its underwriters, the banks that sell the shares to investors. The share count and price range are still blank.
Because Anthropic first filed confidentially in June, SEC rules require the paperwork to be public for 15 days before the roadshow, the marketing tour where banks pitch the shares to investors, which puts the earliest start at November 10.

articles.title: Binance Taps Half Its SAFU Bitcoin, Releases Reserve Proof
articles.text:
Binance taps half its SAFU Bitcoin holdings, releases reserve proof
Binance’s SAFU Bitcoin wallet now holds about 7,500 BTC after a 7,499 BTC transfer linked to the hack, with no timeline for restoring the $1 billion fund.
Binance’s publicly disclosed emergency Bitcoin wallet held roughly half its previous balance on Monday after the exchange tapped its user protection fund to cover losses from Thursday’s $6.3 billion hack.
The exchange confirmed a transfer of 7,499 Bitcoin (BTC) on Saturday, linking it to the partial deployment of its Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU).
As of Monday, the wallet held about 7,500 BTC, worth $583 million, down from about 15,000 BTC before the transfer.
The theft, the largest in cryptocurrency history, forced Binance to suspend withdrawals while it worked to replace the stolen assets. The FBI attributed the attack to North Korea on Saturday, identifying the hackers as TraderTraitor.
Binance began reopening withdrawals in phases on Sunday and said it had replenished approximately 95% of the affected assets, up from 90% a day earlier. It continued buying the remaining, less-liquid tokens through market and over-the-counter transactions.
The exchange is using its corporate treasury, SAFU and part of its futures insurance fund to cover the losses.
SAFU policy sets no deadline to replace funds used after hacks
Binance’s SAFU policy outlines regular monitoring and rebalancing of the fund’s market value.
“If the fund’s market value falls below US $800 million due to BTC price fluctuations, Binance will rebalance the fund to restore its value to $1 billion,” it states.
Related: Binance hackers begin swapping stolen Solana tokens for Bitcoin: Chainalysis
The policy does not specify a timeline for replenishing funds withdrawn following a security incident.
Binance did not immediately respond to Cointelegraph’s questions about SAFU’s remaining reserves, further deployments and plans to replenish the fund.
Binance releases verification proof for post-hack reserves
Binance said Monday that users could now verify their balances against its Saturday proof-of-reserves snapshot after it completed the accompanying cryptographic proof.
The exchange said the snapshot showed customer holdings in 10 cryptocurrencies, including Bitcoin, Ether and USDT, were backed at least 1:1.
The exchange plans to take another snapshot covering more tokens on Wednesday, with the accompanying proof expected to take another 40 to 50 hours to generate.

articles.title: Bitcoin Firm Strive Climbs Up the Treasury Ranks With Another Big Buy - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Strive bought 124 BTC for about $10 million between Oct. 24 and Oct. 30 at an average of $80,526 each, bringing its total to 43,124 BTC.
- The purchase leaves Strive fourth among public companies, 390 BTC behind Twenty One Capital and 876 BTC behind Metaplanet, per Bitcoin Treasuries.
- Most of the buy came from existing cash, and Strive tapped its new SATS preferred stock program for the first time.
Strive, the Dallas-based company co-founded by Vivek Ramaswamy, now holds 43,124 Bitcoin after buying 124 BTC more last week. That stash is now worth roughly $3.3 billion, and good for about 0.2% of the 21 million coins that will ever exist.
That leaves it fourth among publicly traded companies, 390 coins behind Twenty One Capital (which holds 43,514 BTC) and 876 BTC behind Metaplanet (which holds 44,000 BTC), according to Bitcoin Treasuries data.
At Bitcoin’s price of about $77,000, those gaps are worth roughly $30 million and $67 million, respectively.
Will Strategy hold over 1M BTC before 2027?
Strive is a Bitcoin treasury company—a publicly listed firm that keeps Bitcoin on its balance sheet, so anyone with a brokerage account can get exposure by buying its stock. Michael Saylor’s Strategy popularized the playbook back in 2020, and several other companies followed suit, including Strive.
Its coins cost an average of $87,785 each, or $3.8 billion in total, against a market value of $3.5 billion on Oct. 23, per its prospectus. Bitcoin has slipped since, so the pile is now worth a bit less than Strive paid for it.
The latest purchase covers Oct. 24 through Oct. 30 and was disclosed today in an SEC filing, the report US-listed companies must submit when something material happens. Strive paid about $10 million, an average of $80,526 per Bitcoin including fees, CEO Matt Cole said on X.
Strive acquired 124 $BTC for $10M at an average cost of $80,526 per bitcoin, bringing total holdings to ₿43,124.⁰⁰- Existing cash funded most purchases⁰- SATS ATM used for first time, representing 100% of weekly ATM proceeds⁰- Amplification Ratio: 62.7%⁰⁰$ASST $SATA $SATS pic.twitter.com/rFrS6y4AVc
— Matt Cole (@ColeMacro) November 2, 2026
Most of the money came from existing cash, which fell from $504.4 million to $490.4 million over the week. Strive also raised money for the first time by selling shares of a new security called SATS on the open market, Cole said, and that made up all of the week’s fundraising. It still holds 505,000 shares of Strategy’s preferred stock, known as STRC, worth about $50 million.
SATS is a preferred stock—a type of share that pays a fixed dividend before common shareholders see anything. Strive sold 7 million of them at $90 each in an October offering that raised about $630 million, and they carry a 15% annual dividend on a $100 stated value, paid every business day from Nov. 9.
On Oct. 26, Strive opened an at-the-market program—a way to sell new shares in small batches at the going price—for up to $1 billion more SATS. The prospectus says Strive expects to pay the dividends mainly by raising more capital, including selling more shares. The company has set aside 18 months of dividends in a reserve and reported no debt as of Oct. 23.
Strive’s amplification ratio, the preferred stock and debt it carries measured against the value of its Bitcoin, stood at 62.7%, or about $62.70 of obligations for every $100 of Bitcoin.
The company’s CEO has said ending 2026 as the second-largest public Bitcoin holder is possible. “I wouldn’t say that’s my base case,” Cole said on the One Chair podcast in September, “but I would say it’s in the possible set of cards.”
Saylor’s Strategy holds 849,327 Bitcoin, nearly 20 times Strive’s pile.
Twenty One Capital still holds the same 43,514 Bitcoin it had when co-founder Jack Mallers stepped down as CEO in July. His exit came as a plan by Tether to merge three Bitcoin businesses collapsed. The stock had fallen more than 80% from its highs, and his successor, Raphael Zagury, has said Twenty One should be judged on cash flow and capital discipline.
Metaplanet, a Tokyo-listed company that pivoted from hotels to Bitcoin in 2024, holds 44,000 Bitcoin after overtaking mining firm MARA in April. It has a stated goal of 100,000 by the end of 2026.
At last week’s pace of 124 Bitcoin, Strive would pass Twenty One in four weeks and Metaplanet in eight, assuming neither company buys more.

articles.title: FATF Targets Crypto Hubs in Money Laundering Review
articles.text:
FATF targets crypto hubs in review of money laundering controls
The watchdog has not named the jurisdictions under review. Initial findings on compliance with its crypto standards are due in June 2027.
The Financial Action Task Force (FATF) is launching a targeted review of jurisdictions with significant crypto activity to address gaps in how governments apply global anti-money laundering standards.
On Friday, the FATF, an intergovernmental body that sets global standards to combat money laundering, announced that the review would focus primarily on jurisdictions with “materially important” virtual asset service provider (VASP) activity, taking their existing assessment status into account.
The watchdog said its regular assessments and follow-up procedures would remain the main tools for evaluating compliance.
Initial findings will be published in June 2027, with further results in October 2027. The review will also be followed by monitoring and faster reporting to track progress in addressing deficiencies.
The FATF did not name the jurisdictions it would review or say how many would be included. Cointelegraph contacted the watchdog for further details but had not received a response by publication.
The move follows a July FATF report showing that 83% of surveyed jurisdictions had adopted crypto Travel Rule legislation, while significant enforcement gaps persisted.
The report found that 55 of the 91 jurisdictions with Travel Rule laws had yet to take supervisory or enforcement action over compliance. Authorities also struggled to identify unlicensed crypto businesses and oversee providers serving local customers from overseas.
The Travel Rule requires crypto service providers to share information about the sender and recipient of transfers.
Related: FATF urges faster crypto AML enforcement as stablecoin crime increases

articles.title: Mystery $106 Million Crypto Theft Hits EU Entity Days After Binance Hack - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- An unnamed EU entity is suspected of losing more than $106 million from multiple centralized exchange accounts on Nov. 1, ZachXBT said, with the funds withdrawn as USDC and USDT.
- The thief has since swapped stablecoins for ETH, used instant exchanges, converted funds to Monero and bridged assets across chains.
- ZachXBT said with “a high degree of confidence” that the attacker isn’t North Korea’s Lazarus Group, setting the theft apart from the $6.4 billion Binance hack.
Another nine-figure theft has hit crypto, just days after the biggest heist in the industry’s history.
An unnamed entity in the European Union is suspected of losing more than $106 million from several of its accounts on centralized exchanges on Sunday, pseudonymous onchain investigator ZachXBT said Monday in a post to his Telegram channel.
The funds were withdrawn as USDC and USDT stablecoins by what he called an “illicit actor.”
SOL next move: Pump to $160 or Dump to $40?
In the 24 hours that followed, the actor moved aggressively to cover their tracks, ZachXBT said. The attacker swapped USDC for ETH, sent funds through instant exchange services such as WellWallet and Kyrrex, converted some to the privacy coin Monero via Wagyu and bridged assets across multiple blockchains.
ZachXBT published 11 Ethereum addresses tied to the theft.
Instant exchanges let users quickly swap one cryptocurrency for another, often with little identity verification, while Monero hides senders, receivers and amounts, making it a popular tool for obscuring stolen funds.
Swapping out of USDC and USDT also matters because the companies behind those stablecoins can freeze them.
ZachXBT said the culprit remains unidentified, but that he could say “with a high degree of confidence” that it isn’t Lazarus Group, citing multiple laundering indicators. Lazarus is the umbrella name often used for North Korea’s state-backed hackers. ZachXBT didn’t name the victim.
That sets the theft apart from the record-setting $6.4 billion Binance hack, which the FBI has attributed to TraderTraitor, a North Korean hacking group.
In that case, stablecoin issuers moved within minutes. Tether froze stolen USDT on Ethereum in 37 minutes, and Circle froze all $823 million in stolen USDC, helping lock up about 44% of the haul, according to blockchain analytics firm Elliptic.
North Korea’s launderers have since spread the remaining funds across about 12,000 wallets. It’s unclear whether any funds in the EU case have been frozen.
The incident adds to an already unprecedented week for crypto security. Beyond the record-breaking Binance hack, Brazilian exchange Mercado Bitcoin just today reported halting withdrawals after a $40 million hack of its own. Likewise today, BTCPay Server told merchants to switch off their servers amid reports of hot wallet attacks.

articles.title: Binance Hackers Swap Stolen Solana Tokens for Bitcoin
articles.text:
Binance hackers begin swapping stolen Solana tokens for Bitcoin: Chainalysis
Crypto exchange Gate said it froze two linked accounts as US investigators urged platforms to block transactions tied to the $6.3 billion theft.
The hackers behind Binance’s $6.3 billion theft have begun converting stolen Solana tokens into Bitcoin after largely emptying the wallets used to launder funds on Tron, according to blockchain investigators.
Lookonchain reported Sunday that the hackers had moved 486,970 Solana (SOL) tokens, worth about $46.4 million, and were swapping them for Bitcoin (BTC) through Relay.
The activity involves funds that escaped the freezes imposed after Thursday’s theft, the largest in cryptocurrency history. Industry partners, including Tether and Circle, froze about $3 billion in stolen assets, while investigator SomaXBT estimated the attackers still controlled about $3.5 billion.
Binance said the attack compromised its hot wallets, with early findings pointing to a hacked employee laptop before investigators identified additional breach points. The exchange began restoring withdrawals Sunday, pledged to cover the losses and has been working with US authorities to trace and recover the stolen assets.
Related: OKX draws $445M in net inflows as Binance outflows exceed $7B
Chainalysis said Sunday that most of the hackers’ temporary holding wallets on Tron had been emptied as laundering activity expanded to Solana. It put the value of the Tron transfers at about $500 million.
The $500 million figure counted transfers during laundering, including repeated movements between wallets, SomaXBT said in response. About $242 million actually left the Tron holding wallets, he said.
Chainalysis said Friday that hackers may be using automation to obscure the trail, citing thousands of transactions in a short period. The firm observed funds circulating repeatedly between wallets, sometimes returning to addresses used earlier in the sequence.
Source: Chainalysis
FBI asks crypto services to block hackers’ transactions
Some stolen funds also reached centralized exchange Gate. Lookonchain reported Monday that the hackers had deposited about $250,000 there over the preceding 12 hours.
Gate subsequently said it had frozen two linked accounts and would cooperate with law enforcement. Its statement did not specify how much money was frozen.
The FBI on Saturday attributed Thursday’s theft to North Korea’s TraderTraitor hackers and published wallet addresses linked to the stolen assets.
The agency, US Secret Service and IRS Criminal Investigation urged THORChain node operators, exchanges and decentralized finance (DeFi) services to block transactions involving those addresses or funds traced back to them.
Investigators had observed the hackers converting stolen assets primarily into Ether (ETH) and expected further laundering through DeFi and instant swap services, the FBI said.

articles.title: Bitcoin Posts Consecutive October Losses, Defying Uptober
articles.text:
From Uptober to Hacktober: Are Bitcoin’s seasonal patterns becoming obsolete?
Bitcoin lost 7.3% in October 2026 after another decline the previous year, despite the month’s historically strong returns, as analysts reassess seasonal signals.
Bitcoin’s back-to-back October losses have put its “Uptober” reputation under the microscope as analysts weigh seasonal trends against institutional demand and economic conditions.
Bitcoin fell 7.3% in October 2026, following a roughly 4% decline a year earlier, according to CoinGlass data.
The losses defied October’s historically bullish reputation, which earned it the nickname “Uptober.” This year, industry figures turned to darker labels, including “Black October” and “Hacktober,” amid a wave of crypto security incidents, including Binance’s record-breaking $6.3 billion hack.
Bitcoin’s seasonal trends shift as monthly volatility declines
October has historically delivered Bitcoin’s highest median return at 15.4%, with gains in 10 of 13 years through 2025, according to Andrew Yang, a researcher at crypto analytics firm Kaiko.
September’s historically bearish reputation has weakened as well. Bitcoin has posted gains every September since 2023, which could reflect traders buying ahead of an expected October rally, Yang told Cointelegraph.
Bitcoin’s narrowing price swings may also be making seasonal trends less pronounced, Yang said. Its typical monthly move has declined from 14% between 2013 and 2016 to 9.6% since 2024, leaving less room for sharp seasonal rallies, he added.
Are institutions rewriting Bitcoin’s calendar?
Analysts also pointed to institutional investment and broader economic conditions as increasingly important influences on Bitcoin’s price.
Justin d’Anethan, head of research at Arctic Digital, pointed to exchange-traded fund (ETF) flows and corporate Bitcoin buyers, saying their investment decisions are shaped more by liquidity, interest rates and investment mandates than seasonal trading narratives.
Related: Bitcoin ETF flows give mixed read on institutional demand: CoinShares
US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded $515 million in net outflows in October, while spot Ether ETFs saw a record $1.61 billion in monthly withdrawals.
Yang cautioned that spot Bitcoin ETFs, approved in January 2024, are too recent to assess. Still, Bitcoin “increasingly trades like a macro asset, driven more by economic data and institutional flows than by the calendar,” he said.
Two October losses don’t settle the question
Despite two consecutive October losses, analysts cautioned against writing off Uptober entirely.
Julio Moreno, head of research at CryptoQuant, said October has generally performed better during Bitcoin bull markets and worse during bear markets, making the broader market cycle an important factor when comparing returns.
“Price performance depends more on spot demand dynamics than cyclical patterns, and demand doesn’t care about the calendar,” Moreno told Cointelegraph.
Related: Bitcoin risks worst October in 12 years as tech sell-off spreads to gold
Markus Levin, co-founder of XYO, said that traders may be anticipating seasonal gains earlier. “When enough people expect a rally in October, the rally gets priced in before the month arrives,” he said.
“Uptober has historical validity but, like other seasonality metrics, it can also fail at times,” said Arctic Digital’s d’Anethan.
Magazine: Cybersecurity’s Black October: How to protect yourself

articles.title: Claude-Built Linux Exploit Targets Bug That Ubuntu Still Hasn't Patched - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Anthropic says Claude wrote an attack that gives a stranger full control of a Linux server over the internet, using a bug that has existed since Linux version 4.4.
- Red Hat released fixes on Sunday, Nov. 1, but Ubuntu still lists every version from 16.04 to 26.10 as vulnerable.
- The Go Security Team says the best fix is to upgrade to a patched kernel, and warns the bug is not limited to the feature Anthropic's attack used.
Another day, another exploit from ChatGPT or Claude that gives us the chills.
Anthropic says its AI wrote a working attack that lets a stranger take full control of a Linux server over the internet, no password needed. The bug behind it, CVE-2026-98432, has been hiding in Linux since version 4.4 and scores 9.8 out of 10 for severity.
Linux runs countless servers, and Ubuntu is one of its most popular flavors. Ubuntu's own tracker still lists every version from 16.04 to 26.10 as vulnerable.
#1 Searched Person on Google 2026?
Anthropic described the attack on Oct. 27 in a research post covering five targets: Chrome, Safari, Android, Windows, and Linux. Claude wrote the Linux exploit after initial prompting, using an unreleased internal model.
The attack takes less than an hour to find a hidden spot in the computer's memory, then five more minutes to run a command with the highest level of access, known as root.
The flaw works like reading a sticky note after someone already shredded it. One part of the system throws away a piece of information while another part is still using it, per AlmaLinux. A specially crafted message that opens an internet connection can set that off.
Failing costs the attacker almost nothing. "An enabling property of this race condition is that a lost race only fails the handshake without crashing the whole system," Anthropic wrote, "so a determined attacker can retry indefinitely until they succeed."
Anthropic's version needs a server using a feature called multipath TCP, which lets one connection travel over several routes at once. Programs written in Go have switched it on by default since Go 1.24, per the Go Security Team.
But the bug is not limited to that feature. "While the demonstrated exploit requires the target system to expose an MPTCP listener, the underlying bug is not specific to MPTCP," the Go Security Team wrote.
Red Hat released fixes for RHEL 8, 9 and 10 on Sunday, including RHSA-2026:93412. Debian, SUSE, Oracle Linux and Amazon Linux have also shipped fixes, at least for some versions.
For anyone who can't update yet, Red Hat published a temporary firewall rule. It "reduces exposure to this vulnerability but cannot fully prevent it," Red Hat says in its security bulletin. A full working solution is still under development.
Anthropic's earlier Claude Mythos model helped Mozilla find 271 bugs in Firefox, as Decrypt reported in April.
Ubuntu's tracker shows fixes in progress for 22.04, 24.04, 26.04 and 26.10. Versions 20.04, 18.04 and 16.04 show only "Vulnerable," and the tracker gives no release date for any fix.

articles.title: Tom Lee Calls Bottom on AI Stock Selloff, Citing Tight Supply and Crypto Resilience - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Tom Lee told CNBC he thinks the AI stock selloff has reached its bottom, arguing that supply remains tight.
- He pointed to crypto’s reaction to the Binance hack as evidence that much of the selling pressure may already have passed.
- Strong AI demand has not insulated chipmakers from earnings concerns, and Bitcoin fund outflows show investors are still pulling money out.
Fundstrat co-founder and Bitmine chairman Tom Lee says the AI stock selloff has reached its bottom, arguing that demand remains constrained by supply and that crypto’s response to a multibillion-dollar hack suggests investors have already done much of their selling.
“I think we're at the bottom,” Lee said in a CNBC interview on Squawk Box. His call follows a decline that has spread beyond individual AI companies: large technology stocks also sit inside the funds many people use to invest for retirement. (Disclosure: Tom Lee is one of several investors in Dastan, Decrypt’s parent company.)
Lee acknowledged how difficult it is to identify the point where prices stop falling. “Bottoms are dangerous because you don't know how much more downside you have at the bottom,” he said.
His case rests on a distinction between an industry struggling to expand fast enough and one that has built more capacity than customers need.
“The market for AI is still very tight. It's not an overcapacity market,” Lee said. Constraints on spending, including political opposition, are slowing growth without signaling that the boom has peaked, he argued.
Strong demand still leaves earnings problems
The distinction matters for companies building the infrastructure behind AI, including data centers, the facilities that house the computers running these systems. A shortage can leave customers waiting, but it can also prevent suppliers from turning orders into revenue.
Intel offered a particularly sharp example on Friday, when its shares plunged nearly 30% to $65.76 after a disappointing fourth-quarter forecast. Its data center and AI revenue had risen 78% from a year earlier to $7.3 billion, yet manufacturing constraints limited its ability to meet demand.
Intel projected quarterly revenue of $15 billion to $16 billion, with the midpoint about $1.6 billion below analysts’ expectations. Its weaker PC business added pressure, showing why healthy AI demand can coexist with a falling share price.
AI bros and crypto bros are on the same ship
Lee’s second argument looks outside the stock market. He pointed to crypto’s relatively limited response to the Binance security breach, which the exchange initially estimated had an impact of about $6.3 billion.
“If crypto is a leading indicator for risk, you've already seen people sort of washed out,” he said. In his reading, a market that absorbs bad news without a much larger decline may have fewer sellers left to push prices down.
Bitcoin did fall about 4% to roughly $76,400 on Friday, and more than $1.3 billion in positions funded with borrowed money were forcibly closed. U.S. spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds, which hold Bitcoin and trade like stocks, also shed $643.2 million that day, their largest daily outflow of October.
That said, a 4% drop can happen even during bull runs and it is considered a relatively normal occurrence among crypto traders.
Binance said on Friday that about $3 billion of the affected assets had been frozen and pledged to cover losses using its emergency reserve and company funds.

articles.title: Trezor Raises Wallet Passphrase Limit to 128 Characters
articles.text:
Trezor lifts password ceiling after Coldcard’s $100M wallet thefts
Trezor cited July’s Coldcard attacks, in which strong passphrases helped protect some users whose wallet recovery information was compromised.
Hardware wallet maker Trezor has increased the maximum length of optional wallet passphrases from 50 to 128 characters.
On Sunday, Trezor said the change is available in its Trezor Suite with updated device firmware. Older firmware still limits passphrases to 50 characters.
According to Trezor, a passphrase acts like an additional password that users set alongside their wallet’s recovery phrase. An attacker who obtains the recovery phrase would still need the correct passphrase to access funds in that wallet.
Trezor cited the Coldcard attacks in July, when a firmware flaw caused some devices to generate recovery phrases with insufficient randomness, allowing attackers to reconstruct them. Trezor said strong, unique passphrases protected some affected users.
The update follows a separate warning involving Trezor’s own devices.
On Friday, the company advised customers who bought wallets from former authorized reseller CryptoBilis since March to move their funds to new wallets.
An Indonesian customer reported a suspected implant inside a Trezor Safe 5 that could capture on-screen information, including recovery phrases, and transmit it over a cellular network. Trezor said Friday it had not examined the device and had received no reports of related losses.
Related: FBI blames North Korea for record $6.3B Binance hack

articles.title: North Korea Is Laundering Binance Hack Loot at One New Wallet Every 25 Seconds - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- About 44% of the $6.43 billion stolen from Binance has been frozen or seized, Elliptic said, after Tether and Circle moved within minutes to lock up stolen stablecoins.
- The attacker has used about 12,000 wallets and more than 40,000 transactions in under four days, which Elliptic calls automation, not AI.
- About $3.24 billion remains in addresses linked to the theft, and Elliptic expects a months-long cash-out through OTC brokers.
North Korean hackers are moving the $6.4 billion they stole from Binance at a blistering clip: roughly one new crypto wallet every 25 seconds.
In under four days, the attacker has spread the funds across about 12,000 wallets on 11 blockchains in more than 40,000 transactions, according to an analysis published Monday by blockchain analytics firm Elliptic.
But stablecoin issuers moved even faster. About $2.85 billion, or 44% of the haul, has been frozen or seized, compared with roughly 3% after North Korea’s $1.5 billion hack of Bybit in February 2025.
Ethereum next move: Pump to $3K or Dump to $1.5K?
Speed mattered because stablecoins made up $3.46 billion, or 54%, of the haul, and their issuers can freeze them. Tether froze the stolen USDT on Ethereum 37 minutes after it reached the attacker’s wallet, and Circle froze all $823 million in stolen USDC before any of it could be swapped, Elliptic found.
Before the freezes landed, the hacker swapped 434 million USDT for ETH on decentralized exchanges such as Uniswap, borrowed 19,762 ETH on lending protocol Aave against another 59.9 million USDT, and traded 234 million USDT for Tron’s TRX token. In all, about $786 million in stablecoins got away.
Attackers began draining Binance’s hot wallets late Thursday. The FBI has since attributed the theft to TraderTraitor, a North Korean state-linked hacking group, and published hundreds of linked addresses.
Binance, which has pledged to cover all losses, reopened withdrawals Sunday and saw about $3.64 billion in net outflows in the first nine and a half hours.
The laundering that followed has been relentless. On Tron, which became the main route, activity peaked at about 1,300 transactions in a single hour.
That pace fueled speculation that AI agents were doing the work. Elliptic disagreed, pointing to fixed timing, set amounts, blind retries and pauses that resemble human working hours. The firm wrote that while the laundering is clearly automated, “nothing we have seen shows an AI agent making decisions.”
About $3.24 billion remains in addresses linked to the theft, mostly ETH and the 18,270 stolen Bitcoin, which haven’t moved since the day of the attack. Elliptic believes those funds are very likely still held by North Korea, while money already being laundered may have passed to Chinese money-laundering networks.
Only a negligible amount appears to have been cashed out. About $16 million has also flowed to addresses holding proceeds of September’s Bitget exploit.
Based on the Bybit playbook, Elliptic expects the attacker to swap its ETH for Bitcoin in small batches and cash out through over-the-counter brokers over a period of months. Further freezes will be harder, the firm said, since ETH and Bitcoin can’t be frozen. The best remaining chances lie with centralized services, where the funds will eventually have to surface.
The Binance theft caps a punishing stretch for crypto security. BTCPay Server urged merchants to switch off their servers amid reports of hot wallet attacks on Monday, and Brazilian exchange Mercado Bitcoin halted withdrawals after a $40 million hack. It’s unclear whether either incident is connected to the Binance attack.
