articles.title: Binance can cut a winning Bitcoin hedge even when customer assets are backed
articles.text:
Quick Take
- Binance's November 2 update says users can verify Bitcoin backing in its October 31 snapshot.
- Binance says only surplus futures reserves were reallocated; the disclosure does not establish higher ADL probability.
- ADL can reduce profitable futures positions, while eligible Delta Neutral accounts receive lower queue priority rather than immunity.
Binance's latest reserve proof addresses whether a customer's Bitcoin is backed at a dated snapshot. A futures hedge faces a separate test: Binance's futures rules allow Auto-Deleveraging, or ADL, to reduce a profitable short that was offsetting the holding.
In its Nov. 2 proof-completion update, Binance said holders of ten named tokens, including Bitcoin, could independently verify backing of at least 1:1 for the snapshot taken at 00:00 UTC on Oct. 31.
The exchange had disclosed in its Oct. 31 recovery update that some futures insurance reserves helped replenish assets stolen in its security incident. Binance said it released only excess above its required coverage level and that the remaining funds exceeded that requirement. The disclosure alone establishes neither a reserve shortfall nor a measurable increase in ADL probability.
Binance also distinguished its Futures Insurance Funds from user assets: they are its own reserves, outside the user-verifiable PoR view. Those reserves support the handling of bankrupt futures positions and reduce the need to close opposing traders' positions.
Binance said it monitors those funds against stress scenarios and adds company funds when required.
How a profitable hedge can be reduced
The futures insurance FAQ describes several pools assigned to different contract categories, with Binance able to change allocations. An exchange-wide reserve figure therefore cannot automatically describe the protection available to every Bitcoin contract.
The same FAQ defines Maximum Takeover Capacity as a cap on the notional, or face, value of bankrupt positions a fund can absorb at a time. It is a multiple of the fund's current balance, with the predetermined multiplier kept confidential.
That capacity limit differs from the amount available to absorb losses. Its FAQ says ADL can be engaged when takeover capacity is reached or when unrealized losses on positions assumed by the fund exceed the relevant available balance. Waiting for a fund balance to reach zero would miss the capacity constraint described in its guidance.
Neither the amount released nor the information needed to calculate current contract-specific headroom is established by the reallocation disclosure.
Under the ADL priority rules, opposing profitable positions can be selected when the fund cannot accept a bankrupt position. Profitability and leverage affect their place in the queue. A position can therefore be winning on price and still be selected for reduction.
Consider a purely hypothetical trader holding 1 BTC and a linear futures short of 1 BTC. Assume the short has become profitable after a price decline. If ADL cuts it to 0.5 BTC while the underlying holding stays unchanged, only half the holding remains offset.
| Assumed position | Before reduction | After reduction | 
|---|---|---|
| Bitcoin holding | 1 BTC | 1 BTC | 
| Linear futures short | 1 BTC | 0.5 BTC | 
| Net long price exposure | 0 BTC | 0.5 BTC | 
If Bitcoin then falls by an assumed $10,000 per BTC, the remaining combined position loses $5,000 on that further move. That calculation assumes spot and futures move together, quantities remain fixed and the trader adds no replacement hedge. It excludes fees, funding, basis differences, taxes and collateral changes.
The $5,000 is an incremental loss after the reduction, not the strategy's total profit or loss. Whatever the closed portion earned does not provide an ongoing offset to later price changes in the holding.
For positions governed by Binance RCH's clearing rules, an ADL-selected position can be reduced or closed at the triggering bankrupt position's bankruptcy price, without specific consent from the affected clearing participant.
This differs from the collateral problem in CryptoSlate's October analysis of fragmented hedges, where an underfunded losing leg can be liquidated while profits sit elsewhere. ADL can remove the profitable opposing leg. Either mechanism can separate positions that were intended to work together.
Account eligibility changes priority
Binance's Delta Neutral Account guidance offers qualifying hedged positions lower ADL priority within the same profit/loss category. It does not exempt those positions from ADL.
Initial qualification requires Portfolio Margin or Portfolio Margin Pro, VIP4 or above and an enabled Delta Mode for the individual account. The gap between the calculated long and short exposures must be less than 5% of the larger side, expressed as a relative difference below 0.05. Enabling a master account does not enable its subaccounts.
The calculation recognizes eligible assets in Cross Margin and Futures accounts, Cross Margin debts and futures positions. Assets in the Spot Account and options positions are excluded. A Bitcoin holding and an offsetting futures short may form an economic hedge without automatically qualifying for this special queue treatment.
There is also a distinction between entry and continuing eligibility: the FAQ says a later fall below VIP4 alone changes nothing, while disabling Portfolio Margin disables Delta Mode.
Contract scope matters alongside account status. Within the Binance RCH rulebook, ADL applies contract by contract: a position in one contract type is not used to cover losses in another. Those rules refer to Default Funds and tie potentially affected positions to the relevant fund's coverage and available capacity.
The FAQs are educational guidance that defer to governing rules and contract specifications. The applicable Binance entity, product terms and account arrangement determine which legal protections govern a position.

articles.title: Proton Users Revolt After CEO Calls Security Caution 'Loser Thinking' Amid AI Push - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Proton users are reporting subscription cancellations and calling for CEO Andy Yen to resign.
- Yen reportedly called a request for additional security testing “loser thinking” while pushing faster AI adoption.
- The company canceled planned AI re-interviews, then published a manifesto defending its engineering overhaul.
Proton users are reporting subscription cancellations after revelations that CEO Andy Yen pressured engineers to embrace AI and dismissed a request for more security testing as “loser thinking.”
The Swiss privacy company has since canceled planned employee assessments of AI use.
The backlash cuts into Proton’s main selling point—trusting it with information people want kept private. Its encrypted email service scrambles messages to protect their contents, and customers questioning its development practices are asking whether faster releases could come at their expense.
A Proton employee asked the company in August for a few days to pentest new code, meaning specialists would try to break into it before release, per 404 Media. Yen replied: “That’s bullshit and loser thinking. Of course it’s possible to be fast and secure.”
He also urged staff to stop writing code by hand and use more AI, and mentioned that he’d be reinterviewing its staff to see if and how they are using AI to do their job, the outlet reported. Its investigation drew on nine current and former employees, internal messages, and meeting recordings.
This didn’t land well among users, and customers have responded with cancellation notices and demands for new leadership on social media such as Reddit. A proposal on Proton’s feedback forum calling for Yen to step down had 2,020 votes when reviewed, alongside comments from users saying they had canceled subscriptions or would not renew.
Besides the blind use of AI, some former and current Proton employees on Reddit and social media have documented a toxic work culture, especially from the CEO.
Those posts document anger, rather than a verified count of departing customers. Canceling a paid plan also does not necessarily mean deleting an account.
Proton’s AI ambitions predate this dispute. Its Lumo chatbot comes with protections against using conversations to train AI, but internal use of AI was not among Proton’s selling points, even in the peak of the chatbot hype.
To address concerns over irresponsible use of AI, on November 1, technology chief Bart Butler published an engineering manifesto arguing that developers should direct large language models, AI systems that generate text and code, rather than treat them as occasional assistants.
Butler compared manual coding to memorizing phone numbers, and envisioned eventually ending most human code review. He also insisted that expertise and testing remain essential, with engineers accountable for work that models cannot reliably handle.
“Your job has fundamentally changed. It is no longer to write code, and LLMs are not here to help you write better code faster,” the manifesto reads. “Your job is to help the LLM write better code faster.” Doubling on its stance, Proton sees avoiding AI as an “existential threat” to the success of its very mission.
“‘Programming’ is dead. Engineering is not,” Buttler told his own team. “Your old job is gone”.
The document also calls for company-wide investment in automation, arguing that generating code faster achieves little if approvals and other development steps remain slow. Butler described that overhaul as the next phase of adoption.
AI tools can introduce security problems of their own. For example, Microsoft researchers said a now patched Claude flaw could expose secret access credentials through malicious instructions hidden in material the coding assistant reviewed.
They can also help find weaknesses: Google’s PageBreak system searches its applications for exploitable bugs and checks whether attacks actually work.
Proton acknowledged to 404 Media that management had sometimes communicated too bluntly and that employees were anxious. Its public manifesto nevertheless argues that failing to adopt AI quickly threatens the company’s ability to compete.
Yen canceled the re-interviews on October 30. The assessments would have required staff to explain their AI use, with employees fearing their answers could determine whether they kept their jobs.

articles.title: Hong Kong Enables 24/7 Tokenized Settlements, Plans Stablecoin Trials
articles.text:
Hong Kong takes tokenized settlement to 24/7, plans stablecoin trials
The HKMA plans to bring regulated stablecoins into tokenized government debt trials, while HSBC says its RedCoin stablecoin has reached 50,000 users.
Hong Kong has expanded its Project Ensemble pilot to allow round-the-clock settlement of tokenized transactions, as the city’s monetary regulator prepares to bring regulated stablecoins into trials involving tokenized government debt.
On Monday, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) said that it had advanced its EnsembleTX project to a new stage allowing 24/7 real-value transactions. The HKMA said the update would help banks and their clients move funds globally, manage tokenized investments and handle treasury operations outside conventional settlement hours.
Participating banks initially settled payments through Hong Kong’s existing dollar settlement system, which limited settlement hours. When the pilot began real-value trials in November 2025, the HKMA said it planned to introduce tokenized central bank money to allow settlement around the clock.
The HKMA launched Project Ensemble in March 2024 to explore how banks could settle tokenized transactions using wholesale central bank digital money. A sandbox opened that August, allowing banks to connect their tokenized deposit platforms and test transactions.
Speaking at Hong Kong FinTech Week on Monday, HKMA Chief Executive Eddie Yue said the regulator was introducing tokenized central bank money as a “foundation layer” for 24/7 settlement. He said tokenized bonds, money market funds and bank deposits were already being used.
The HKMA also said recognized dealers had completed secondary-market trial trades in tokenized Exchange Fund Bills, a form of short-term debt issued by the regulator. It plans to expand those trials to include regulated stablecoins.
HSBC’s RedCoin reaches 50,000 users
Separately, HSBC Group CEO Georges Elhedery said at Hong Kong FinTech Week that the bank’s recently launched Hong Kong dollar stablecoin, RedCoin, had reached 50,000 users about 10 days after its debut.
“We have 50,000 users,” Elhedery said, adding that HSBC was targeting “multi-million users” as it expands access to the token.
RedCoin’s rollout brings stablecoins to retail payments, while Ensemble’s settlement work has focused on transactions involving banks and tokenized investments.
Elhedery said HSBC was also offering tokenized deposits to wholesale clients in Hong Kong and about half a dozen other jurisdictions, allowing funds to move around the clock.
Related: Hong Kong prepares banks for quantum threats amid tokenization push
The bank launched RedCoin on Oct. 23 for transfers and merchant payments through its PayMe application. HSBC said more than 3.3 million PayMe customers could activate stablecoin wallets to use the token. It also plans to bring the stablecoin into its mobile banking app and allow subscriptions to tokenized investments, including a Hong Kong dollar money market fund share class.
HSBC was among Hong Kong’s first licensed stablecoin issuers in April alongside Anchorpoint Financial, a venture backed by Animoca Brands and Standard Chartered. The city’s licensing regime, introduced in August 2025, requires issuers to meet standards for backing reserves, redemption and risk management.

articles.title: Tom Lee calls Ethereum’s 4% post-hack fall bullish
articles.text:
Quick Take
- Tom Lee calls Ethereum's roughly 4% decline after Binance's hack a sign that a crypto bull market is underway.
- His 20% Bybit comparator covers a full week, while the Binance figure covers only the days since Oct. 29.
- BitMine added 8,573 ETH and held 6,060,506 tokens as of Nov. 1, giving the company a direct financial interest in Ethereum.
Tom Lee believes crypto's muted reaction to Binance's $6.3 billion hack is another sign that a bull market is underway.
The BitMine chairman pointed to Ethereum's roughly 4% decline following the Oct. 29 theft, which was more than four times larger than the $1.5 billion stolen from Bybit in February 2025.
Ethereum fell 8% on the day the Bybit breach was disclosed and extended its losses to 20% within a week, according to Lee. The 20% comparison covers a full week after Bybit, while the Binance figure covers only the days since Oct. 29.
In a Nov. 2 statement, Lee described the latest market reaction as “very constructive,” arguing that the industry's response to an unprecedented security breach reflects growing resilience.
The prices quoted in BitMine's releases show Ethereum fell approximately 17% between Oct. 4 and Nov. 1.
Why Lee believes the hack shows crypto's growing strength
Lee cited six factors behind the relatively subdued market response, including Binance's ability to cover customer losses, swift intervention by stablecoin issuers and the absence of cascading failures across decentralized finance platforms.
The exchange initially committed more than $6 billion in company funds to cover the stolen assets, seeking to reassure customers that the theft would not leave them exposed to losses.
By Nov. 2, Binance said it had replenished approximately 95% of the affected assets using its own funding sources, including its corporate treasury and insurance reserves.
Binance also said users could independently verify that ten major cryptocurrencies, including Bitcoin, Ethereum, XRP and BNB, were backed at least 1:1 in its Oct. 31 proof-of-reserves snapshot.
Blockchain analytics firm Elliptic verified approximately $2.85 billion in frozen or seized assets, accounting for 44% of the theft.
Tether and Circle were among the companies that restricted compromised tokens, while other issuers and blockchain networks took similar measures.
Lee also highlighted the speed of the criminal investigation. The FBI identified North Korea's TraderTraitor hacking group as responsible within two days, compared with previous incidents in which attribution took considerably longer.
Another distinction was the nature of the breach. Investigators have linked the Binance incident to compromised corporate infrastructure, rather than a failure in Ethereum or another blockchain's underlying protocol.
BitMine's Ethereum holding
BitMine has continued buying Ethereum despite its recent downturn.
The company acquired another 8,573 ETH during the latest reporting week, lifting its holdings to 6,060,506 tokens, equivalent to approximately 4.9% of Ethereum's circulating supply.
However, the value of its broader portfolio of crypto assets, cash, marketable securities and other investments declined from $17.4 billion on Oct. 4 to $14.5 billion on Nov. 1, despite the continued accumulation.
Elliptic estimated on Nov. 2 that approximately $3 billion remained in addresses linked to the theft, mostly as Bitcoin and Ethereum.
Binance is also working to source the remaining 5% of affected customer assets, comprising less-liquid tokens, while preparing another proof-of-reserves snapshot for Nov. 4.

articles.title: Nvidia and Nike Lead Biggest Wave Yet of Tokenized Stock Objections - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Twelve more companies, including Nvidia, Costco and Nike, objected to trading of their shares on OKXICE TSV, according to its Oct. 30 notice, the largest batch yet.
- The total has climbed from nine on Oct. 15 to 50, spanning tech, finance, retail, health care and energy.
- Under the SEC’s innovation exemption, a timely objection bars the venue from listing a third-party tokenized version of a company
Even Nvidia doesn’t want its shares on OKX and ICE’s planned tokenized stock venue.
The chipmaker is among 12 new companies listed as objecting issuers in an updated notice from OKXICE TSV dated Friday. The others are Costco, Nike, Micron, CrowdStrike, Palo Alto Networks, Reddit, Hewlett Packard Enterprise, Corning, Bloom Energy, IREN, and USA Rare Earth. The additions bring the total to 50 companies.
Tesla and SpaceX merger officially announced by...?
It’s the largest single batch yet. The list stood at 38 in the venue’s Oct. 28 notice, when Walmart and Eli Lilly joined, and at nine when the first objectors appeared on Oct. 15. It has more than quintupled since.
The newcomers span chips, cybersecurity, retail, and energy. Nvidia, Micron, and Corning join hardware peers such as AMD, Intel, and Broadcom, while CrowdStrike and Palo Alto Networks bring cybersecurity heavyweights to the list. IREN, a Bitcoin miner that has expanded into AI cloud computing, adds a name from the crypto industry itself.
Under the SEC’s innovation exemption, which the agency unveiled in September after the Clarity Act stalled in the Senate, a venue must notify a company before offering a version of its shares tokenized by an unaffiliated third party. If the company objects in writing within 30 days, the venue can’t make that stock available for trading, according to the SEC’s order. The objection applies only to that venue.
OKXICE TSV, a 50-50 joint venture between NYSE owner Intercontinental Exchange and OKX’s U.S. holding company, plans to let approved users trade tokenized U.S. stocks around the clock. Trades would run through permissioned Uniswap v4 pools on OKX’s XLayer blockchain, paired with stablecoins such as USDC.
None of the objecting companies have explained their decisions, but Nasdaq offered one possible rationale when it opted its own shares out of the exemption.
A spokesperson told The Wall Street Journal that Nasdaq doesn’t want its stock trading on a venue that doesn’t show the best prices in real time or report trades to the consolidated tape.
Further, Crypto in America reported that Nasdaq may be playing a role behind the scenes in encouraging companies to opt out of the OKX-ICE venture. “Our Nasdaq rep had reached out to us regarding OKX listing, suggesting we should object and that they would hold a call to discuss why,” an executive at a Nasdaq-listed company told the publication. “Nasdaq is definitely partly behind this,” the exec reportedly said.
OKXICE’s notice acknowledges it isn’t subject to Regulation NMS, the rules designed to ensure investors get the best displayed prices. It also warns that broker-dealers face unsettled questions about trade reporting and best execution on the venue.
Some of the market’s biggest names, including Apple, Tesla and Amazon, still haven’t appeared on the list.

articles.title: Bitcoin Price Holds $76.3K Lows Into US Midterms Week
articles.text:
BTC heads into US midterm showdown: Three things to know in Bitcoin this week
Bitcoin price action held its 100-day moving average into the monthly close as crypto markets braced for US midterm election and tech earnings volatility.
Bitcoin (BTC) held above its 100-day moving average on Monday ahead of US midterm elections, jobs data and earnings from Apple and Palantir.
Key points:
- Kalshi traders put Democrats’ chances of winning control of the House at 93.6% ahead of Tuesday’s US midterm elections.
- US nonfarm payrolls are forecast to rise by 65,000 in October as markets favor a December Fed rate hike.
- Bitcoin holds its 100-day moving average as trader Rekt Capital compares its price chart with the 2023 recovery.
Midterms follow Bitcoin’s weakest October since 2014
Tuesday’s US midterm elections will determine control of Congress, with prediction market traders heavily favoring a Democratic victory in the House of Representatives.
Kalshi put the probability of Democrats winning the House at 93.6% as of Monday.
President Donald Trump said he would use his veto power if Democrats took control of Congress.
“I guess I’ll become Mr Veto. They’ll be sending stuff up. You veto it,” he said, according to the New York Post.
US midterm elections odds (screenshot). Source: Kalshi
Bitcoin ended the fourth quarter lower in each of the past three US midterm election years, falling 17.3% in 2014, 43.5% in 2018 and 14.8% in 2022. All three periods coincided with Bitcoin bear markets.
Benjamin Cowen, founder and CEO of crypto analytics platform IntoTheCryptoverse, suggested that the midterms can function as a cue to increase BTC exposure due to their short-term bearish impact on price.
“Usually the Q4 dump of midterm years just provide opportunities to buy for those who sold long ago,” he said Friday on X.
In July, Cowen referenced Bitcoin bear-market bottoms coinciding with the second half of midterm years.
BTC/USD was down 6.4% for the quarter as of Monday, after its weakest October since 2014, according to CoinGlass.
BTC/USD liquidation heatmap. Source: CoinGlass
Jobs data and tech earnings test market expectations
September US job openings data are due Tuesday, followed by October’s nonfarm payrolls report on Friday.
Payrolls are expected to rise by 65,000, after the economy added 29,000 jobs in September, below forecasts for 84,000. Such an outcome notionally increases the odds of dovish policy signals from the Federal Reserve, which is in turn bullish for crypto and risk-asset liquidity.
Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack and Fed Governor Michelle Bowman are among the officials due to speak this week.
Data from CME Group’s FedWatch Tool currently shows that markets expect the Fed to raise interest rates by 0.25 percentage points at the December meeting of the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC). The odds of such an outcome have sat between 67% and 75% for the past month.
Fed target rate probability comparison for December FOMC meeting (screenshot). Source: CME Group
The University of Michigan will also release its preliminary November consumer sentiment survey on Friday, including consumers’ inflation expectations.
Alongside the macro data prints, 20% of S&P 500 companies are due to report earnings in the coming days. Chief among these are tech giants Apple and Palantir, both due to report after the market close on Monday.
The reports follow last week’s tech sell-off, when disappointing guidance renewed concerns about AI spending and profitability.
Economist Mohamed El-Erian described markets as now “acutely sensitive” to tech-sector news headlines in weekend analysis.
“The market is particularly focused on justification for the massive capital expenditures being deployed across the sector, ROI’s, and revenue growth,” he wrote.
Bitcoin chart draws comparisons with 2023 recovery
After closing October down 7.3%, Bitcoin is holding above a moving average that has provided support since mid-August.
Related: Here’s what happened in crypto today
TradingView data showed BTC/USD staying above last week’s low near $76,300, without retesting it around the monthly close.
That low was close to the 100-day simple moving average (SMA) for BTC/USD, which has since risen to $76,548.
Bitcoin also reclaimed its 100-week exponential moving average (EMA) in time for the monthly close, with this standing at $77,759.
BTC/USD daily chart with 100 SMA, 100 EMA. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView
Trader and analyst Rekt Capital compared the weekly chart with Bitcoin’s rebound from its 2022 bear market low. During the recovery, BTC/USD produced an inverse head-and-shoulders pattern, retested support at the right shoulder, briefly fell below it and then rallied.
Last week’s drop to $76,300 brought Bitcoin back to what Rekt Capital identified as right-shoulder support on the current chart. He is watching for a brief move below that level as a possible next step in the comparison.
“The question now is whether Bitcoin can produce some sort of downside deviation below here over the next few weeks,” Rekt Capital said.
BTC/USD one-week chart. Source: Rekt Capital on X.com

articles.title: Binance warns of second wave of crypto theft as $6.3 billion hack recovery continues
articles.text:
Quick Take
- Binance has warned of fresh scam risks as withdrawals resume following its $6.3 billion hack.
- Fraudsters could exploit withdrawal delays through fake compensation offers, phishing links and malicious wallet approvals.
- Binance says 95% of affected assets have been replaced, but withdrawals remain restricted as another reopening phase approaches.
Binance has warned customers about potential scams exploiting withdrawal delays as the exchange recovers from a $6.3 billion security breach.
In a Nov. 2 security advisory, the exchange said fraudsters could take advantage of its phased withdrawal reopening by impersonating Binance representatives and offering customers assistance with delayed transactions, compensation claims and asset recovery.
The warning covers fraudulent emails, direct messages, group chats and even small cryptocurrency transfers carrying malicious instructions.
According to Binance, scammers may promise to speed up pending withdrawals, sell customers priority access to withdrawal queues, or instruct them to transfer their holdings into supposedly secure wallets.
The exchange emphasized that it does not charge fees to unlock withdrawals, offer paid recovery services or ask customers to authorize wallet transactions to regain access to their funds.
It also warned against fraudulent proof-of-reserves websites and compensation eligibility links, which could become particularly deceptive as the exchange introduces new verification tools following the breach.
Once customers approve malicious wallet permissions, attackers can transfer their assets without further authorization, potentially creating losses that cannot be reversed.
The warning comes as Binance attempts to restore normal operations after an Oct. 29 attack that compromised its hot wallets and resulted in approximately $6.3 billion in stolen cryptocurrencies.
Binance verifies major crypto reserves as recovery remains incomplete
Meanwhile, Binance announced on Nov. 2 that it had completed the zero-knowledge proof for its Oct. 31 reserve snapshot, allowing customers to independently verify the backing of ten major cryptocurrencies.
The covered assets include Bitcoin, Ethereum, BNB, XRP, Solana, Zcash, and four stablecoins: USDT, USDC, USD1, and RLUSD.
Binance said the completed proof lets customers verify that their balances were included in the snapshot and backed by reserves of at least 1:1, without revealing individual account holdings.
The process requires users to obtain account-specific verification information and download a verification tool through Binance's official proof-of-reserves platform.
However, the verification applies to balances recorded at 00:00 UTC on Oct. 31 and does not establish the exchange's current financial position or independently audit its overall solvency.
The announcement also comes as Binance continues replenishing assets affected by the theft.
According to the exchange, approximately 95% of the impacted assets have been replaced using company resources, while the remaining 5% consists of less-liquid cryptocurrencies that are more difficult to acquire in sufficient quantities.
Binance has been sourcing those assets through market purchases and over-the-counter transactions, separately from efforts to trace and recover the original stolen funds.
The exchange began restoring withdrawals on Nov. 1, with access returning progressively across supported cryptocurrencies and blockchain networks.
Another phase is scheduled for Nov. 3, although Binance has yet to confirm which additional assets and networks will become available.
The prolonged reopening gives fraudsters an opportunity to exploit customers awaiting access to their funds, particularly through fake support channels and requests for wallet authorizations.
Binance has instructed customers with pending withdrawals to check their status directly through its application and verify suspicious communications using its official verification service.
The exchange plans to publish another reserve snapshot on Nov. 4 covering additional cryptocurrencies. Generating the accompanying zero-knowledge proof is expected to take another 40 to 50 hours.

articles.title: Elon Musk Mocks Sam Altman Over Claim Home PCs Are Wasting RAM - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said it is "quite terrible" for the world's limited supply of DRAM to sit in home computers that are used 5% of the time.
- Elon Musk mocked the comments on X with a meme of the Nazi officer Hans Landa from Inglourious Basterds accusing people of "withholding DRAM from the cloud."
- The exchange is the latest clash between the two OpenAI co-founders, after a jury rejected Musk's $150 billion lawsuit against OpenAI in May.
Elon Musk has mocked OpenAI CEO Sam Altman for arguing that the world's limited supply of computer memory would be better used in AI data centers than in people's home computers.
Altman made the comments in an interview with the YouTube channel Cheeky Pint, while discussing the shortages of memory and other components caused by the AI boom.
"A lot of people want local inference, and somehow they assume that the problem is solved now because we're going to have open-source models," Altman said, referring to running AI models on a user's own hardware. "But from like a global allocation perspective, actually, it's quite terrible to have everybody have a bunch of the world's limited supply of DRAM sitting in their own computer and being used 5% of the time."
"You want maximum utilization in a cloud if you're trying to deal with this very supply-constrained environment," he added. "And somehow, many people's intuition is the opposite of that."
Musk responded on X on Sunday with a meme showing Hans Landa, the Nazi officer played by Christoph Waltz in the film Inglourious Basterds, captioned: "You are withholding DRAM from the cloud, are you not?" "The people deserve to have their RAM too!" Musk wrote alongside the image.
The people deserve to have their RAM too! pic.twitter.com/q6dwauALw4
— Elon Musk (@elonmusk) November 1, 2026
In the interview, Altman blamed the shortage partly on memory makers' caution. For years, a DRAM producer "would invest $20 billion of CapEx to make $19 billion," he said, and companies that nearly went bankrupt building too many factories in past cycles have been slow to expand, even as they now stand to generate huge profits.
Altman said he would like to see prices for energy, chips and the rest of the supply chain fall. "If it doesn't go down, I'll be very sad," he said, adding that for prices to fall, supply needs to grow.
Tesla and SpaceX merger officially announced by...?
Musk versus Altman
The jab is the latest in a long-running feud between the two men, who co-founded OpenAI with others in 2015 before Musk left in 2018.
Musk sued OpenAI and Altman in 2024, accusing them of abandoning the organization's founding nonprofit mission. In May, a federal jury in California rejected the $150 billion lawsuit, finding OpenAI, Altman and president Greg Brockman not liable on all claims. OpenAI's lawyers had argued that the suit was motivated in part by competition, after Musk launched rival AI company xAI in 2023.

articles.title: OKX Leads Crypto Exchanges with $445M in Daily Inflows
articles.text:
OKX draws $445M in net inflows as Binance outflows exceed $7B
OKX led cryptocurrency exchanges with $445 million in daily inflows, while Binance processed about $7 billion in net outflows.
OKX recorded about $445 million in 24-hour net inflows, the largest among tracked crypto exchanges, while Binance continued to register outflows after reopening withdrawals following its $6.3 billion hack.
Crypto exchange Bybit was in second place with $112 million in net inflows, followed by Gate with $91 million and Bitget with $54 million in 24-hour net inflows, according to DefiLlama.
Binance recorded the biggest net outflows among tracked exchanges, with more than $7 billion, up from $5.8 billion earlier Monday. Binance said it began restoring withdrawals in phases at 6:00 a.m. UTC on Sunday.
At the time of writing, Binance held about $127.9 billion in wallets tracked by DefiLlama, more than four times the $29 billion at OKX, the second-largest exchange by that measure.
Binance suspended withdrawals Friday, soon after late Thursday’s $6.3 billion hack, the largest in cryptocurrency history.
By Sunday, Binance said it had replenished approximately 95% of the affected assets, up from 90% on Saturday. The remaining 5% consisted of less liquid tokens that it continued to buy through market and over-the-counter transactions.
The exchange is using its corporate treasury, a partial deployment of its Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU) and a portion of its futures insurance fund to replace the stolen assets. Binance has pledged to absorb the losses without passing them on to customers.
About $3 billion in stolen assets frozen by industry partners is separate from Binance’s replacement funds. Binance said Sunday it published a new reserves snapshot and an updated proof-of-reserves report was expected Monday.
OKX’s OKB token rose about 1.4% over the past 24 hours to trade near $113 on Monday, while BNB gained 0.3% to about $708 over the same period, according to CoinMarketCap.

articles.title: Tether freezes $4.5 million as Mercado Bitcoin hacker holds $46 million in crypto
articles.text:
Quick Take
- Mercado Bitcoin said it suspended deposits and withdrawals preventively after quickly containing a security incident in one system.
- No customers suffered losses and no data leaked, according to @MercadoBitcoin; neither statement quantified the incident’s financial extent.
- Mercado Bitcoin’s restoration update shared tracking addresses but gave no reopening timetable, while its status page showed a partial outage.
Tether has frozen more than $4.5 million in USDT linked to a security breach at Brazilian crypto exchange Mercado Bitcoin.
Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino confirmed the freeze on Nov. 2, saying the stablecoin issuer blocked more than 4.5 million USDT linked to the incident.
Notably, Tether is a major investor in the exchange. The stablecoin issuer announced a $20 million strategic investment in Mercado Bitcoin in July to support its expansion into tokenization, payments, and other digital financial services.
Meanwhile, on-chain analyst Specter reported that coordinated efforts involving security researchers and stablecoin issuers had expanded the immobilized assets to more than $9 million across nine digital assets, including USDC, PAXG, RLUSD, and others.
The intervention came as blockchain analytics firm Arkham Intelligence identified approximately $46 million in cryptocurrency held by wallets attributed to the attacker, including $8.37 million in Ethereum, $8.24 million in Bitcoin and $1.76 million in PEPE.
Earlier today, Mercado Bitcoin disclosed that it had identified and contained a security incident affecting one of its systems overnight.
The exchange temporarily suspended deposits and withdrawals while investigating suspicious asset movements but maintained that customers suffered no financial losses and that no personal information was compromised.
However, it has not disclosed the financial extent of the attack or explained whether its corporate reserves were affected.
Mercado Bitcoin subsequently published suspicious destination addresses across Bitcoin, Ethereum-compatible networks, Solana, Stellar and Tron to support tracing and potential recovery efforts.
Centralized crypto exchanges face growing wave of security breaches
The Mercado Bitcoin breach comes less than four days after hackers stole a record $6.3 billion from Binance on Oct. 29, extending a series of major attacks against centralized crypto exchanges.
Binance's incident followed a $388 million security breach at Bitget on Sept. 24, when attackers siphoned assets from the exchange's wallet infrastructure. Bitget subsequently tapped its protection fund to absorb the losses and protect customer balances.
The attacks have revived concerns about the security of centralized trading platforms, which collectively custody billions of dollars in digital assets and depend on internal systems to authorize transfers.
A similar pattern emerged in 2025, when two major exchanges suffered substantial losses within weeks of each other.
In February, Bybit lost approximately $1.5 billion after hackers manipulated the transaction approval process for one of its Ethereum cold wallets. The incident followed a $69 million hot-wallet breach at Phemex in January.
Although the incidents involved different attack methods, they exposed vulnerabilities in wallet management, transaction authorization, and the infrastructure exchanges rely on to safeguard customer assets.
The North Korean-linked TraderTraitor operation has been implicated in the two largest attacks. The FBI attributed both the Bybit and Binance thefts to North Korean hackers, demonstrating how sophisticated threat actors have repeatedly targeted centralized custodians.
However, investigators have not established any connection between those operations and the latest Mercado Bitcoin breach.

articles.title: Brazil's Largest Exchange Mercado Bitcoin Halts Withdrawals After $40 Million Hack - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Mercado Bitcoin suspended deposits and withdrawals on Monday after a security incident, saying customers lost nothing and no data leaked.
- Blockchain security firm Hypernative flagged more than $40 million in suspicious transfers across at least 10 blockchains; the exchange has not confirmed that figure.
- Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino said the stablecoin issuer froze more than 4.5 million USDT tied to the incident.
Brazil's largest crypto exchange, Mercado Bitcoin, suspended deposits and withdrawals on Monday after identifying a security incident in one of its systems in the early hours of the morning. The exchange said no customer lost money and no data leaked.
"We identified and quickly contained a security incident in one of our systems early this morning," Mercado Bitcoin said in a Portuguese-language statement on X. "As a preventive protection measure, deposits and withdrawals are temporarily suspended."
Blockchain security firm Hypernative flagged more than $40 million in suspicious transfers that may be linked to the incident, according to a preliminary analysis that spans at least 10 blockchains, including Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, and Tron. Mercado Bitcoin has not confirmed that figure and has not disclosed how the attackers got in.
In a follow-up post, the exchange published the destination addresses it identified on five networks: EVM chains (blockchains built to run the same code as Ethereum), Bitcoin, Solana, Stellar, and Tron. It said the addresses were released only so others can identify and track the funds on-chain.
Comunicado oficial:
Identificamos e contivemos com rapidez um incidente de segurança em um de nossos sistemas nesta madrugada.
Reforçamos que:
• Não houve nenhum prejuízo aos clientes;
• Não houve vazamento de dados.
Como medida preventiva de proteção, depósitos e saques…
— Mercado Bitcoin (@MercadoBitcoin) November 2, 2026
Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino said in a post on X that the stablecoin issuer has frozen more than 4.5 million USDT connected to the incident.
USDT is a dollar-pegged stablecoin, and Tether can blacklist the addresses holding it so the tokens cannot be moved, though a freeze does not by itself return the funds to their owner.
Tether froze more than 4.5M USDT related to this security incident. https://t.co/PCtP4957jn
— Paolo Ardoino 🤖 (@paoloardoino) November 2, 2026
The incident comes days after hackers drained more than $6 billion from Binance on October 29, a theft the FBI attributed to North Korea's TraderTraitor group. Binance has since reopened withdrawals and said it replenished about 95% of the affected assets. Mercado Bitcoin has not linked the two incidents and has not said who is behind its own.
Deposits and withdrawals at Mercado Bitcoin remain suspended, and the exchange has not given a date for resuming them. It said it will post regular updates on X.

articles.title: Strategy’s deployable cash falls 45% as buybacks outpace Bitcoin purchases
articles.text:
Quick Take
- Strategy bought 811 BTC for $66 million while spending a record $208 million on STRC preferred-stock buybacks.
- Deployable USD Cash fell 45% to $133 million despite $164 million in common-stock proceeds; $99 million of those proceeds went into that cash balance.
- Strategy separately held a $4.79 billion reserve for preferred dividends and debt interest, distinct from cash available for broader treasury uses.
Strategy‘s deployable USD Cash fell 45.3% during the week ended Nov. 1, from $242 million to $133 million, as preferred-stock buybacks exceeded its Bitcoin purchases.
That balance is available for broader treasury uses. Strategy also held a separate $4.79 billion USD Reserve intended for preferred-stock dividends and debt interest.
The company bought 811 Bitcoin between Oct. 26 and Nov. 1 while setting another record for STRC preferred-stock buybacks.
The company spent approximately $66 million acquiring the cryptocurrency at an average price of $80,846 between Oct. 26 and Nov. 1, according to its Nov. 2 regulatory filing.
The purchase increased Strategy's holdings to 849,327 BTC, acquired for an aggregate $64 billion at an average price of $75,451 per coin.
The acquisition marked a return to larger Bitcoin purchases after Michael Saylor's firm suspended buying for a week while concentrating its spending on preferred-stock repurchases.
Strategy had acquired just 334 BTC, 250 BTC and 267 BTC in the first three reporting weeks of October, respectively. Its latest purchase was the largest since Sept. 28, when the company disclosed acquiring 1,665 BTC for approximately $143 million.
Strategy sold approximately 1,178,552 shares of its MSTR common stock through its at-the-market offering program, generating $164 million in net proceeds.
However, only $66 million, or about 40%, went toward purchasing Bitcoin. The remaining $99 million was allocated to the company's deployable USD Cash balance, which has come under pressure from its increasingly aggressive preferred-stock repurchase program.
The company did not issue any new preferred shares during the reporting period, leaving common-stock sales as its only source of fresh equity capital.
Record STRC buybacks drain Strategy's cash
While Strategy resumed accumulating Bitcoin, its spending on STRC continued to accelerate.
The company repurchased approximately 2,092,035 STRC shares for $208 million, surpassing the previous weekly record of $205 million established in late October.
The latest transaction means Strategy spent more than three times as much repurchasing preferred shares as it did acquiring Bitcoin.
It also paid an average of approximately $99.52 per STRC share, bringing the transaction price within 0.5% of the security's $100 stated value. That compares with an average purchase price of approximately $99.06 the previous week.
STRC is a variable-rate perpetual preferred security carrying a 12% annualized dividend rate. Strategy has been purchasing the shares to support their trading price near $100 while reducing the amount of preferred capital outstanding.
Strategy entered the reporting period with approximately $242 million in USD Cash. Despite allocating another $99 million from common-stock sales to that balance, it finished the week with just $133 million after spending $208 million on STRC repurchases.
That represents a $110 million, or 45.3%, weekly decline in deployable cash.
The separate USD Reserve declined from approximately $4.83 billion to $4.79 billion after the company used $43 million to pay preferred-stock dividends during the reporting week. The reserve remains substantially larger than its flexible cash balance but serves a different purpose under the company's capital management framework.
Strategy has spent more than $2 billion on preferred-stock repurchases since it launched the program in July.
The company has about $749 million in remaining authorization under its expanded $3 billion digital credit securities repurchase program, along with an unused $1 billion authorization to repurchase MSTR common shares.

articles.title: Bitcoin ETFs End October Red, Ether ETFs Lose Record $1.61B
articles.text:
Bitcoin ETFs sink into October outflows with $643M exit after Binance hack
US spot Bitcoin ETFs ended October with $515 million in net withdrawals, while Ether funds posted a record $1.61 billion in monthly outflows.
Investors pulled $643 million from US-listed spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds (ETFs) on Friday, pushing October’s net flows into negative territory as crypto markets faced volatility following Binance’s $6.3 billion hack.
Friday’s withdrawals snapped four consecutive days of inflows, leaving the funds with $515 million in net outflows for October, their first negative month since June, according to SoSoValue. The funds still attracted approximately $361 million in net inflows for the year through October.
BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) led Friday’s outflows with $234 million, followed by Fidelity’s Wise Origin Bitcoin Fund (FBTC) with $201 million, according to Farside Investors data.
The withdrawals followed Bitcoin’s drop to $77,000 on Thursday. Binance, the world’s largest crypto exchange by trading volume, confirmed Friday that hackers had stolen about $6.3 billion in crypto assets.
Hardware wallet maker OneKey’s founder and CEO, Yishi, warned on X Friday that IBIT could face similar security threats because it relies heavily on Coinbase to hold its Bitcoin.
Investors also withdrew a net $156 million from US spot Ether (ETH) ETFs on Friday, bringing October’s net outflows to a record $1.61 billion. The previous monthly high was $1.42 billion in November 2025.
October’s withdrawals also erased the Ether funds’ net inflows for 2026, leaving them with roughly $45 million in net outflows for the year.
Related: Bitcoin risks worst October in 12 years as tech sell-off spreads to gold

articles.title: Bitmine Buys More Ethereum as Tom Lee Calls the Binance Hack Bullish - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Bitmine bought another 8,573 ETH, raising holdings to 6,060,506 ETH (about $13.7 billion), or 4.9% of supply—99% of the way to its “Alchemy of 5%” goal.
- Chairman Tom Lee argued the record $6.4 billion Binance hack showed crypto’s resilience, citing six reasons for the muted 4% ETH drop.
- Total holdings hit $14.5 billion; Bitmine remains the top ETH treasury and No. 2 behind Strategy, resumed buying with a $66 million purchase.
Bitmine Immersion Technologies kept its weekly Ethereum buying streak intact, adding 8,573 ETH worth roughly $19 million, while chairman Tom Lee used the record Binance hack to argue that crypto has grown more resilient, not more fragile.
The NYSE-listed company said Monday its holdings now total 6,060,506 ETH, worth roughly $13.7 billion at a reference price of $2,261 per coin.
Ethereum next move: Pump to $3K or Dump to $1.5K?
That represents 4.9% of Ethereum’s 122.2 million token supply, leaving Bitmine, by its own count, 99% of the way to its goal of owning 5% of the network, a target it brands the “Alchemy of 5%,” reached in just 15 months. The firm has bought Ethereum every week since launching its treasury strategy on June 30, 2025.
Most of Lee’s commentary focused on last week’s roughly $6.4 billion theft from Binance, which the FBI has attributed to North Korea. Lee called it “a terrible development” but argued the market’s “relatively muted” reaction was “very constructive.” (Disclosure: Tom Lee is one of several investors in Dastan, Decrypt’s parent company.)
Lee noted that when North Korea’s Lazarus-linked hackers drained $1.5 billion from Bybit in February 2025, Ethereum fell 8% that day and 20% within a week, whereas ETH slid just 4% after the Binance breach, despite the theft being roughly four times larger.
Lee laid out six reasons for the muted response: Binance’s ability to cover all customer losses, the absence of a cascade of DeFi failures like the one that followed Bybit, swift industry action that cut the potential loss in half, the FBI naming North Korea within two days rather than the months such attributions have taken historically, the fact that the exploit was a “corporate infiltration” of Binance’s infrastructure rather than a blockchain flaw, and the limited price downside itself, which he read as a sign a “crypto bull market is underway.”
Taken together, he said, the episode shows the industry is “increasingly resilient and more capable of absorbing these nation-state assaults.”
Counting cash, other tokens and what it calls “moonshot” investments, Bitmine’s total holdings stood at $14.5 billion as of Nov. 1, including 216 Bitcoin, $498 million in cash and marketable securities, a $180 million stake in Beast Industries and an $82 million position in Eightco Holdings, which it bills as a rare public proxy for indirect OpenAI exposure.
Bitmine remains the world’s largest Ethereum treasury and the second-largest crypto treasury overall, trailing only Michael Saylor’s Strategy, which the release said holds about 848,517 BTC.
Strategy recently resumed its own Bitcoin buying with a $66 million purchase after a brief pause.
Bitmine has 5,227,037 ETH, about 86% of its holdings, staked through its MAVAN platform, with projected annualized staking revenue of roughly $358 million.

articles.title: BTCPay Server Identifies Attack Vector After Bitcoin Wallet Theft Reports
articles.text:
BTCPay Server warns of hot wallet thefts running on outdated software
BTCPay Server urged operators to shut down their servers after receiving reports of unauthorized attackers draining funds from hot wallets.
BTCPay Server has identified an attack vector affecting older versions of its payment software after receiving reports of attackers draining funds from users’ hot wallets.
On Monday, the Bitcoin payment platform said its investigation identified an attack vector targeting instances running version 2.4.1 or earlier, which was released July 23, 2026.
The project said it had received no credible reports of hot wallet drains among users running its latest release, version 2.4.7 and urged operators to update their installations.
The findings followed an earlier warning, in which BTCPay urged operators to shut down server instances while it investigated the unauthorized wallet withdrawal reports. It also shared instructions for operators to shut down their servers.
BTCPay has not disclosed the number of affected operators, the value of stolen funds or technical details explaining how attackers accessed the wallets. It asked affected users to submit information and logs to its security team.
Cointelegraph reached out to BTCPay Server for comment but did not receive a response before publication.
The reports come less than three months after BTCPay restricted remote Lightning access following an August attack that exploited a vulnerability to obtain Lightning Network Daemon (LND) credentials and steal funds.
It remains unclear whether the latest attack vector is connected to the August vulnerability.
Related: Binance net outflows surge to $5.8B as withdrawals resume after record hack

articles.title: Vitalik is making private Ethereum payments without a crypto website
articles.text:
Quick Take
- Vitalik Buterin says he uses kohaku-cli for many private payments, alongside a separate AI-written tool for ENS updates.
- Retaining a local wallet revision can reduce repeated website code delivery while leaving package and update decisions with users.
- Railgun unshield preparation can already contain a signed operation, so withholding broadcast does not universally mean withholding a signature.
Vitalik Buterin is moving some of his Ethereum activity out of website interfaces. In his October 31 essay, the Ethereum co-founder said he had used an AI-written command-line tool for recent IPFS content-hash updates on ENS, Ethereum's naming system, and kohaku-cli, a command-line wallet, for many payments through privacy protocols. The ENS updater and payment wallet were separate tools.
His objection goes beyond screen clutter. A website can deliver application code again whenever someone returns, leaving the user dependent on what the server supplies each time. Keeping a local application can reduce that repeated delivery exposure. It also moves a consequential decision onto the user: which software revision to install, retain and eventually replace.
The wallet he linked makes the trade-off concrete. Its documentation warns that the CLI is unaudited, under active development and written with AI assistance. It tells users to avoid mainnet unless they understand what they are doing and the possibility of catastrophic fund loss.
Control over a downloaded interface matters because the accepted code sits between a payment instruction and the signature authorizing it. Choosing when that code changes can reduce one recurring exposure, while its dependencies and signing access determine what the installed software can do.
Keeping a copy changes the delivery decision
The practical gain is the ability to keep a chosen application revision rather than obtaining the website interface again on each visit. Accepting a replacement revision creates another delivery decision. For this source-build route, that decision also involves the dependency set and the tools that turn source into executable software. A familiar project name alone does not describe all the code being accepted.
Kohaku-cli handles public Ethereum accounts and private balances on Tornado Cash, Railgun and Privacy Pools V1. It is a particular wallet application, distinct from the broader Kohaku toolkit of reusable protocol libraries and wallet infrastructure. Its warning should be read at that application level, rather than as an audit verdict on every component or protocol it uses.
The documented installation route also shows what “local” entails. The project's instructions call for installing dependencies with npm install, building the application with npm run build, and running a local launcher. At commit 0ef5c44, the documentation, manifest, lockfile and implementation describe the same application revision. Its manifest identifies version 0.1.0 and requires Node.js 22 or later. Buterin's account does not identify his installed revision.
The manifest fixes direct dependency versions, including viem and several Kohaku packages. It also pins a separate kohaku-artifacts Git dependency to a commit. The corresponding lockfile records resolved registry packages and integrity hashes. The application therefore has a software supply chain even when its interface runs on the user's machine.
Preparation can already involve a signature
Kohaku-cli's public-transfer and Railgun unshield paths show why a pause before submission can mean different things. An ordinary public-transfer dry run returns without sending the transaction; a prepared Railgun unshield can already contain a signature.
For an ordinary, non-batched public transfer, the transfer implementation simulates the transaction and returns dry-run output without submission. The broadcast path requires the sender's private key, constructs a local wallet client and sends the transaction. The wallet-client code derives its signing account from that private key.
Private operations expose an additional wrinkle. The unshield command can output a prepared Railgun UserOperation that is already signed, even when broadcasting is withheld. A UserOperation is an account-operation payload that compatible tooling can submit. The separate broadcast implementation expects a signed operation and then sends it through a Pimlico bundler.
For that path, withholding submission can still leave a signed operation ready for compatible tooling to submit later. Calling the result “prepared” therefore does not make it universally unsigned. Software that may construct an authorization, software that may sign it and software that may submit it need to be assessed as distinct sources of authority, even when one CLI coordinates them.
Human confirmation is another separate choice. In the inspected public-transfer path, a suitably configured caller with wallet access can use --non-interactive together with --broadcast to submit without a further confirmation prompt. Wallet unlocking, required parameters, chain matching and simulation checks still apply. The capability is relevant to scripts and agents; it does not reveal whether Buterin uses unattended payments.
The README describes an encrypted seed on disk and owner-restricted password files for POSIX automation. Those measures govern stored secrets and how a process obtains access to them. They do not, by themselves, establish an independent spending limit or recipient policy once the process can use the signer.
CryptoSlate has previously covered the wallet-permission problem for local AI. Delivery control adds another dimension: a user can retain a chosen interface revision, while that code operates within whatever signing and submission authority it receives.
Provenance checks origin, with a separate question about behavior
Software provenance offers a way to examine the delivery side more rigorously. It records where an artifact came from and how it was built. The SLSA verification standard describes checking a provenance signature, matching the artifact's digest, recognizing a trusted builder and comparing the stated source and build parameters with expected values.
These checks can help distinguish an expected build from a substituted artifact or an unintended build source. They still depend on which builders and source expectations the verifier trusts.
Dependency checking remains its own task. SLSA describes recursive verification of resolved dependencies as an optional additional step. Authenticating the top-level artifact does not automatically authenticate every input to it.
Correct origin and build history can accompany application logic that the user would still reject.
Network privacy is similarly separate from application delivery. The CLI documentation describes Tor by default for certain non-RPC traffic while Ethereum RPC stays on the ordinary network connection. Running the interface locally therefore does not make every external interaction private. Earlier Kohaku and verified-RPC coverage concerned another part of this broader trust problem.
Buterin's experiment points to a concrete form of user control: choosing the application code that stays on the machine and deciding when to accept replacement code. Its value depends on carrying that control through dependency selection and the signer.

articles.title: Bank of Korea Probes Banks’ Exposure to Crypto Hacks
articles.text:
Bank of Korea probes financial firms’ exposure to crypto risks
The central bank is surveying 31 financial institutions on how a major exchange shutdown, prolonged crypto downturn or losses at another firm could affect their operations.
The Bank of Korea has reportedly asked banks and brokerages about cryptocurrency-related risks, asking how they would be affected by a major exchange hack, a market crash or heavy losses at another financial institution.
The central bank began surveying 18 banks and 13 brokerages on Oct. 23 as part of its first reported review of financial institutions’ participation in the virtual asset market, according to The Herald Business and Yonhap, citing financial industry sources.
The survey includes questions about each institution’s crypto-related staffing and budgets, business activities and reasons for entering the market, along with amounts invested in domestic and overseas crypto companies.
One scenario asks how financial firms would be affected if South Korea’s largest crypto exchange by market share temporarily suspended operations following a major hack or similar incident.
Other questions address a steep fall in cryptocurrency prices followed by a sustained trading slump, and the potential fallout if another financial institution suffered heavy losses from a crypto-related incident.
The survey began before last week’s $6.3 billion Binance hack, but the incident highlights the type of risk the central bank is examining. US authorities have attributed the attack to North Korean hackers.
Responses are reportedly due on Wednesday.
South Korean banks explore stablecoins amid regulatory delays
The review comes as South Korean financial firms have continued testing stablecoin services.
KB Financial Group completed a won-denominated stablecoin pilot in May, while Kakao Pay and KakaoBank partnered with Fireblocks in September to explore digital asset infrastructure.
The Bank of Korea has pushed for bank-led stablecoin issuance, while disagreements over which institutions should be permitted to issue stablecoins have complicated progress on the proposed Digital Asset Basic Act.
“Financial institutions are making their own preparations even as virtual asset legislation is moving more slowly than the market expected,” a Bank of Korea official told The Korea Herald.
Regulators have also stepped up cybersecurity scrutiny. In October, the Financial Services Commission proposed tougher security requirements after finding deficiencies at 130 of 555 financial companies.
The proposals include more frequent vulnerability assessments and greater executive accountability, following security incidents involving 16 companies, including crypto exchanges.
Related: FBI blames North Korea for record $6.3B Binance hack

articles.title: Arthur Hayes wants to hedge AI compute bills, but FLOP token swings could change the cost
articles.text:
Quick Take
- Arthur Hayes proposes dollar-settled futures for AI compute costs using a FLOP-priced index and a currency-covariance adjustment.
- For buyers acquiring FLOP when they consume inference, token conversion and model mismatch can leave dollar costs exposed.
- FLOP remains a development network, while its draft standardized forwards face profile, economics and physical-pilot activation gates.
Arthur Hayes’s proposed AI-compute futures could offset a rise in a FLOP-priced benchmark while leaving a dollar-funded buyer exposed to the token’s exchange rate. The distinction affects businesses that would buy FLOP as they pay for inference, the work of running AI models to generate answers.
His October 26 blueprint connects financial contracts to FLOP Network, where AI agents would pay for model responses with the planned FLOP token. Receiving dollars from a hedge would stabilize the buyer’s dollar bill only to the extent that the contract matches its workload and currency exposure.
Hayes explicitly recognizes the currency link. He says pricing these proposed quanto contracts requires an adjustment for covariance between the compute index and the FLOP-dollar exchange rate, meaning how the two move together. Pricing that relationship and matching a particular customer’s bill are separate tasks: model choice, currency funding and purchase timing can leave residual exposure.
The market remains proposed. FLOP’s GPU-provider guide, updated October 30, says it operates only as a development network and involves no real money. Its official status page says no real FLOP token is trading.
When the dollar payoff matches the bill
Hayes calls the underlying index the Flop Reference Compute Rate, or FRCR. His essay labels it an hourly volume-weighted FLOP/GigaFLOPS rate and outlines quarterly futures and perpetual swaps that entrepreneurs could bring to traditional-finance or crypto exchanges.
The proposed quarterly contract uses USD margin and a multiplier of $1 per index point. A buyer going long one contract at 100 points would earn $100 if it settled at 200, before costs. That payment follows the change in the numerical index.
For a buyer acquiring tokens as it consumes inference, the bill has an additional conversion. It needs enough FLOP to purchase the workload and pays the dollar cost of acquiring those tokens. Even if the workload’s FLOP price follows FRCR exactly, the dollar bill also depends on the exchange rate at purchase.
The proposal also needs a settled measurement convention. FLOP tokens are currency; floating-point operations measure work; operations per second measure throughput. Hayes’s printed expression dividing a fee by work and then by latency does not dimensionally match a price per unit of throughput. The examples below therefore use numerical index points and an assumed workload relationship, rather than treating that expression as a verified conversion into physical compute.
Consider a hypothetical buyer whose fixed workload costs 100,000 FLOP when the index is 100. Assume its FLOP bill moves in direct proportion to that index. At an invented exchange rate of $1 per FLOP, the starting dollar bill is $100,000.
Give the buyer 1,000 long futures contracts entered at 100 points, each with Hayes’s proposed $1-per-point multiplier. For this example, that position offsets a proportional increase in the workload’s FLOP price when the token exchange rate stays at $1.
These scenarios let the numerical index and the FLOP-dollar exchange rate move independently for a buyer acquiring tokens as it consumes inference. A maintained dollar anchor could change that relationship, while prepaid forward purchases set token-acquisition costs upfront.
| Hypothetical settlement | Index | USD per FLOP | Dollar inference bill | Futures gain | Bill minus gain | 
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Index doubles; token unchanged | 200 | $1 | $200,000 | $100,000 | $100,000 | 
| Index unchanged; token doubles | 100 | $2 | $200,000 | $0 | $200,000 | 
| Index doubles; token halves | 200 | $0.5 | $100,000 | $100,000 | $0 | 
In the first case, the futures gain returns the net outlay to the original $100,000. In the second, the dollar bill doubles without an index move, so the futures pay nothing. In the third, the token’s fall already offsets the higher FLOP-denominated workload price, while the index-linked futures still produce a gain.
The zero is the bill minus that hypothetical gain, before fees, margin cash needs, covariance-adjusted entry pricing, model mismatch, roll costs or default.
FLOP’s present bootstrap pricing has a separate constraint. Its architecture FAQ describes inference prices in FLOP anchored to dollars. A maintained anchor can cause FLOP-denominated prices to adjust as the token exchange rate changes.
Matching the model and the delivery schedule
Currency is only one matching problem. Hayes’s reference rate is a composite, while the forward compute claims used to reproduce it are tied to particular models.
He acknowledges that a trader seeking synthetic FRCR exposure would need model-specific FLOP Compute Units, or FCUs, in the weights matching the index. Changes in the model mix alter that basket. A buyer using one model could therefore face a different price movement from the composite, even before converting FLOP into dollars.
The draft yellow paper defines an FCU as a specified amount of reference work under an identified metering profile and a supported model whose identity is fixed. That convention measures the work in the claim; a GPU’s advertised peak speed measures a different quantity.
Hayes illustrates longer exposure by rolling successive 30-day FCUs and describes perpetual exposure through continuous rolls. That approach depends on being able to replace positions at the required times and prices.
There is also a difference between his blueprint and the current draft specification. Hayes describes up to thirty daily FCU series for each model. The yellow paper instead specifies new standardized primary delivery starts from the next calendar day through fourteen days ahead, with seven days ahead as the default. Booking lead time is separate from the duration of delivery.
The current booking rules therefore qualify how the 30-day rolling example could be implemented. Standardized activation also remains gated on a completed executable profile, calibrated economics and a qualified physical pilot. The implementation matrix describes the FCU path as partial.
Collateral adds another dependency. Hayes’s forward design calls for fully funded purchase offers and provider bonds in FLOP. Backup providers and refunds address missed delivery, but his own description allows for circumstances in which replacement compute cannot be obtained. Receiving tokens back is a different outcome from receiving inference when it is needed.
Currency timing also depends on funding. If a buyer fully prepaid a specified forward claim using FLOP acquired at reservation, the dollar cost of acquiring those tokens would be incurred upfront. That would set the token-acquisition outlay for that purchase, while leaving delivery performance and other costs to be assessed.
The miner manual describes development inference and calibration, but says the SOFT verification tier’s full settlement and dispute path remains open and the HARD-tier bridge is not deployable.
As of November 2, FLOP’s testnet network page still labels the network planned and its release unreleased. The official timetable gives provisional targets of November 3 for testnet and Q1 2027 for mainnet and token generation.
The wider policy work is also exploratory. The CFTC’s August 19 consultation asked about compute cash-market liquidity, manipulation, customer protection and perpetual futures.
Hayes’s blueprint offers a way to transfer exposure to a compute index. For a buyer funding inference as it goes, predictable dollar spending would require the right combination of model-price and currency protection; his proposed rolling replication would also need executable forward rolls. A dollar settlement currency defines the contract’s payment, while the buyer’s purchasing arrangements determine how closely it protects the bill.

articles.title: How T7X Is Building the Infrastructure for a New Era of Capital Markets - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Security tokenization can give holders the economic benefits of share ownership without making them shareholders of record.
- Native issuance places the token inside the security's authorized issuance, with a transfer agent maintaining the record.
- Wyoming law recognizes a "certificate token," letting corporate shares be represented on a blockchain.
Most tokenized stocks aren't natively issued on a blockchain. They begin as conventional shares, sit with a broker or custodian, and are then represented by tokens issued separately. In effect, the market has largely replicated traditional securities structures on-chain instead of rethinking them from the ground up. The token "may track the value of the underlying shares," writes Ivan Kan, CMO of tokenization platform T7X, in an essay shared with Decrypt, "but the token holder is not necessarily the shareholder of record."
While the holder owns the price movement, whether they own the share is another matter altogether. The SEC set out three models in January: issuers tokenizing their own shares, third parties issuing tokens against shares held in custody, and firms issuing a separate security for synthetic exposure.
Writing for Forbes' Technology Council in August, Kan cited Pantera Capital research covering 593 tokenized assets across 11 asset classes, of which 77.6% were what Pantera called "digital wrappers around traditional infrastructure" rather than securities in their own right.
"What does the token legally represent, and who authorized it?" Kan asks, setting out an alternative model that T7X Equities is pursuing, which they dub "native issuance." A security exists because an issuer authorizes it, they argue, and "blockchain does not eliminate those corporate and securities-law requirements."
One token, one security, one issuance
Under the native issuance model, the token is part of the authorized issuance from the start, running from issuer authorization to investor verification to transfer-agent validation, aiming at "one security, one authorized issuance, one ownership record, one digital representation."
Wyoming, Delaware, and Nevada corporate law recognizes a "certificate token," allowing shares to be represented electronically on a blockchain. T7X is incorporated in Wyoming and structures its issuances to operate within this framework. The blockchain then becomes "part of the infrastructure supporting the capitalization table" instead of being just another instrument layered on top.
The transfer agent keeps the official master securityholder file and the blockchain records transactions, while the legal record of ownership stays where regulators expect it.
In T7X's administrated offerings, that transfer agent is T7X Equities. Transfer agents register with the SEC and hold the authoritative record of who owns a security, processing transfers and maintaining the master file, which puts the company inside the model it is advocating as well as behind it. Its first example is Tranquil Healthcare Fund I, a Tier 2 Regulation A+ offering of up to $75 million that the SEC qualified on June 29. T7X Equities issues tokens representing its shares on Trusted Smart Chain and delivers them to investors' wallets, the company said.
"There's a registered, SEC-regulated gatekeeper that determines who owns which security at any point in time," T7X Chief Executive Pablo Penaloza said at Consensus in Miami earlier this year. "As long as you have a transfer agent involved, there is no way that securities can disappear without trace."
RWA+
Kan calls the broader category "RWA+." The plus doesn't refer to any single rule, he argues, but the requirement that "compliance and oversight are real," and it rests on three elements. Native issuance creates the token as part of the security's authorized issuance. Integrated compliance writes investor verification and disclosure into the instrument from the start, not as an afterthought. Legally enforceable ownership puts the token holder on the transfer agent's record.
"A receipt is not an asset," Kan wrote in Forbes. "It is a claim wrapped around one, dependent on an intermediary to honor it." Synthetic "PreStocks" tied to SpaceX and Anthropic were never valid claims, he noted, because neither company authorized the transfers. Done properly, he argues, "ownership, compliance and settlement are the same fact."
Whether a token carries the rights of a share is becoming the dividing line elsewhere, too. The SEC's new innovation exemption covers tokenized stocks carrying dividends and voting rights while excluding price-tracking synthetics, and Nasdaq's arrangement with Kraken turns on tokens conveying the same voting rights as ordinary shares.
Penaloza pins the near-term opportunity on companies raising under $100 million, usually between $50 million and $75 million, through Regulation A offerings.
Regulation A+, Kan argues, suits this model because it permits public solicitation and non-accredited participation while requiring audited financials and continuing disclosure. Most tokenized assets rely instead on Regulation D placements, limited to accredited investors. Reg A also opens the door, Penaloza notes, to retirement accounts. Unregistered securities can legally sit in a self-directed IRA, but many brokers won't hold them and most investment advisers steer clients away. "The money is sitting in the older generations' retirement accounts," he said, and a registration attached to the investment is what makes an individual retiree comfortable holding it.
For investors already holding these securities, the benefit is an exit. Shareholders in Reg A and Reg D placements typically receive a paper certificate and then "have to go around and find somebody who will want to give them liquidity," Penaloza said. A native digital security can trade on a secondary market, he said, settling wallet to wallet without a custodian in between.
Giving Reg A and Reg D holdings somewhere to trade would, he argued, "incredibly speed up not only the rate of capital formation, but also the liquidity in the market." Within five years, he predicts, "the total tokenized portfolio will far surpass the existing market capitalization of what is currently trading on all the public markets."
To find out more about T7X’s real-world asset tokenization platform, head to t7x.com.
